akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿ٱلْمُزَّمِّلُ﴾: the original form is المُتَزَمِّل, but the tāʾ was assimilated (idghām) into the zāy; and ﴿المُدَّثِّر﴾ is like it.

akhfash:2-4.t: And His words ﴿قُمِ ٱلْلَّيْلَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ ﴿نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً﴾ ﴿أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ﴾: one who asked about this said: He has said ﴿قُمِ ٱلْلَّيْلَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾, so how did He say ﴿نِصْفَهُ﴾? The meaning is only "or half of it, or add to it" (أَوْ نِصْفَه أَو زِدْ عَلَيْهِ), because what carries this meaning the Arabs express without "أو" ("or"). You say "أَعْطِهِ دِرْهَماً دِرْهَمَيْنِ ثلاثةً" ("give him a dirham, two dirhams, three"), meaning "or two dirhams or three" (أَوْ دِرْهَمَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاثَةً).

akhfash:8-8.t:
And He said ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلاً﴾: He did not bring its own maṣdar (verbal noun), for its maṣdar is "التَبَتُّل", just as He said ﴿أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾. And the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and forty-third verse cited as evidence]:
وَخَيْرُ الأَمْرِ ما اسْتَقْبَلْتَ مِنْهُ * وَلَيْسَ بِأَنْ تَتَبَّعُه اتِّباعَا
(The best of an affair is what you meet head-on, not that you go trailing after it.)
And he said [in the rajaz metre; this is the two hundred and forty-second verse cited as evidence]:
......................... * يَجْرِي عَلَيْها أَيَّمَا إِجْراءِ
(… it runs upon it — what a running!)
That is because it only ran because it was made to run. «[Translator's note: i.e., the poet uses إِجْراء, the maṣdar of أَجْرى "to make run", with the verb جرى "to run".]»

akhfash:9-9.t: And He said ﴿رَّبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ﴾: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject; lit. "on inception"), and genitive as a badal (substitute).

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿مَّهِيلاً﴾ because you say "هِلْتُه" ("I poured it out"), so "هو مَهِيل" ("it is poured out").

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ ٱلْوِلْدَانَ شِيباً﴾: He made ﴿يَجْعَلُ ٱلْوِلْدَانَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of "the day", and did not make it a genitive construct (iḍāfa), because He left (the returning pronoun) implied. «[Translator's note: i.e., the implied form is "يجعل الولدان فيه شيبًا".]»

akhfash:20-20.t:
And He said ﴿أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَيِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفهُ وَثُلُثِهُ﴾. It has also been read in the genitive, and that is widespread, but the meaning does not accord with it, according to what has reached us, because that would amount to "less than half of it" and "less than a third of it", whereas what He prescribed was a third or more than a third, since He said ﴿قُمِ ٱلْلَّيْلَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ [2] ﴿نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً﴾ [3]. As for the one who read in the genitive, his reading is permissible on the basis that it means — and Allah knows best — that you did not perform what was prescribed for you, so you stood less than two-thirds of the night, and (less than) half of it, and (less than) a third of it.
And He said ﴿تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً﴾ because "هو", "هما", "أنتم", "أنتما" and the like may serve as descriptions (ṣifāt) of pronouns, as He said ﴿وَلَـٰكِن كَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ and ﴿تَجِدوُهُ عندَ اللهِ هُوَ خَيْر﴾; and [sometimes] they make it a noun that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), as you say "رأيتُ عبدَ اللهِ أبُوه خيرٌ مِنْه" ("I saw ʿAbdullāh, his father being better than he"). «[Translator's note: the source text writes «يكنْ»; the second quotation, ending خَيْر, reflects the reading with هو as mubtadaʾ.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ﴾ the Prophet; its underlying form is الْمُتَزَمِّلُ, with the tāʾ assimilated into the zāy, i.e. the one wrapped in his garments when the revelation came to him, out of fear of it because of its awesomeness.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿نِصْفَهُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for قَلِيلًا, its smallness being relative to the whole; ﴿أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ﴾ from the half ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ down to a third,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ up to two-thirds; أَوْ is for giving a choice. ﴿وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ be measured in reciting it ﴿تَرْتِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا﴾ a Quran ﴿ثَقِيلًا﴾ awe-inspiring, or severe because of the obligations it contains.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ rising [to pray] after sleep ﴿هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا﴾ agreement of hearing with the heart in understanding the Quran [وِطَاءً] ﴿وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا﴾ clearer in speech.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا﴾ activity in your occupations, in which you are not free for reciting the Quran.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. say «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ» at the beginning of your recitation, ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ﴾ devote yourself exclusively ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ in worship ﴿تَبْتِيلًا﴾ the maṣdar (verbal noun) of بَتَّلَ, brought for the sake of the verse endings (al-fawāṣil); it is what is entailed by al-tabattul. He is

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا﴾ one to whom your affairs are entrusted.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca, of their harm, ﴿وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا﴾ with no anxious complaint in it; this was before the command to fight them.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَذَرْنِي﴾ leave Me ﴿وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ conjoined to the object, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the meaning is: I will suffice you against them; and they are the leaders of Quraysh; ﴿أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ﴾ of luxury, ﴿وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا﴾ of time; and they were killed a short while after it, at Badr.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا﴾ heavy fetters, plural of نِكْل with kasra on the nūn, ﴿وَجَحِيمًا﴾ a burning fire,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ﴾ which chokes in the throat: it is al-zaqqūm, or al-ḍarīʿ, or al-ghislīn, or thorns of fire that neither come out nor go down; ﴿وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful, in addition to what has been mentioned, for whoever denied the Prophet ﷺ,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ﴾ quakes ﴿الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا﴾ heaped sand ﴿مَهِيلًا﴾ flowing after having been heaped; it is from هَالَ يَهِيلُ, and its underlying form is مَهْيُول: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was transferred to the hāʾ; the wāw, the second of the two quiescent letters, was dropped because it is augmentative; and the ḍamma was changed to a kasra to suit the yāʾ.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ he is Muhammad ﷺ ﴿شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, for the disobedience that issues from you, ﴿كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا﴾ he is Moses, upon him be blessing and peace;

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا﴾ severe.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ in this world ﴿يَوْمًا﴾ the object (mafʿūl) of تَتَّقُونَ, i.e. its punishment; i.e. with what fortress will you fortify yourselves against the punishment of a day ﴿يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا﴾ plural of أَشْيَب, because of the severity of its terror; and it is the Day of Resurrection. The original vowel of the shīn of شِيبًا is ḍamma, and it was given kasra to suit the yāʾ. Of a severe day it is said: "a day that turns the forelocks of children white", and that is figurative; it is possible that what is meant in the ayah is the literal sense.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿السَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ﴾ possessing infiṭār, i.e. splitting, ﴿بِهِ﴾ by that day, because of its severity. ﴿كَانَ وَعْدُهُ﴾ the Exalted's [promise] of that day's coming ﴿مَفْعُولًا﴾ i.e. it will happen without any doubt.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذِهِ﴾ fear-inspiring ayahs ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ an admonition for creation; ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way, through faith and obedience.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى﴾ less ﴿مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفِهِ وَثُلُثِهِ﴾ in the genitive, conjoined to ثُلُثَيِ, and in the accusative [وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ], conjoined to أَدْنَى; and his standing [in prayer] in that way was like what he had been commanded at the beginning of the sura; ﴿وَطَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ﴾ conjoined to the pronoun of تَقُومُ, and that is allowed without an emphasising [pronoun] because of the separation [between them]; and a group of his Companions stood [in prayer] likewise, in imitation of him. Among them were some who did not know how much of the night they had prayed and how much of it remained, so they would stand the whole night out of caution; they stood until their feet swelled, for a year or more, and then it was lightened for them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ﴾ reckons ﴿اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy, its noun omitted, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ﴾ i.e. the night, so as to stand in what is obligatory to stand in, except by standing all of it, and that is hard for you; ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ He turned you back to lightening; ﴿فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ﴾ in the prayer, by praying what is easy. ﴿عَلِمَ أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ travelling ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ seeking of His provision through trade and other things, ﴿وَآخَرُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ and for each of the three groups what was mentioned regarding the night prayer is hard, so it was lightened for them by standing what is easy of it; then that was abrogated by the five prayers. ﴿فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ﴾ as preceded, ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ﴾ the obligatory one ﴿وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by spending wealth other than what is obligatory in the way of good ﴿قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ from a willing heart. ﴿وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا﴾ than what you leave behind; [هُوَ] is a separating pronoun (faṣl), and what follows it, even if it is not definite, resembles a definite noun because it cannot take the definite article. ﴿وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ to the believers.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), and hā is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); and ﴿الْمُزَّمِّلُ﴾ badal (substitute) of أيّ. ﴿قُمِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ an adverb of time; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, like the vocative clause; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative; and ﴿نِصْفَهُ﴾ badal of الليل. ﴿أَوِ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿انْقُصْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of something omitted, its implied form being «a time» (زمانا). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿زِدْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to انقص; and ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَتِّلِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿تَرْتِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿سَنُلْقِي﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ثَقِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ inna and its noun, annexed to الليل; and ﴿هِيَ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause «إن ناشئة..» is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; and ﴿وَطْئاً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿أَقْوَمُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أشد; and ﴿قِيلًا﴾ tamyīz.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿فِي النَّهارِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿سَبْحاً﴾ the postponed noun of inna; and ﴿طَوِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿اسْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿تَبْتِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿رَبُّ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿الْمَشْرِقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْمَغْرِبِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المشرق; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation; and ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿هُوَ﴾ badal (substitute) of the latent pronoun in the omitted khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَاتَّخِذْهُ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَكِيلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلى ما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَاهْجُرْهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; and ﴿هَجْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿جَمِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَذَرْنِي﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). ﴿أُولِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of المكذبين; and ﴿النَّعْمَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمَهِّلْهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; and ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; and ﴿لَدَيْنا﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; and ﴿أَنْكالًا﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿وَجَحِيماً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أنكالا; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَطَعاماً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أنكالا; and ﴿ذا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), annexed to ﴿غُصَّةٍ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَعَذاباً﴾ also conjoined; and ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ an adjective of عذابا.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ an adverb of time, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَالْجِبالُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الأرض; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَكانَتِ الْجِبالُ كَثِيباً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; and ﴿مَهِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of كثيبا; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿شاهِداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of رسولا; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شاهدا; and ﴿كَما﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَخَذْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿أَخْذاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَبِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿تَتَّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making jussive. ﴿كَفَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ the object of تتقون. ﴿يَجْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿الْوِلْدانَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شِيباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) منفطر; the nominal clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of يوما. ﴿كانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; and ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿اتَّخَذَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and ﴿إِلى رَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «اتخذ..» is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من, and the clause of من is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّكَ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿تَقُومُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿أَدْنى﴾ an adverb of time; the verbal clause is the khabar of أنك, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم; and ﴿مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أدنى; and ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدنى. ﴿وَطائِفَةٌ﴾ conjoined to the latent fāʿil of تقوم; and ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of طائفة; and ﴿مَعَكَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the verse has اللَّيْلَ]. ﴿وَالنَّهارَ﴾ conjoined to it; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلِمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ lightened from the heavy, and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) [Translator's note: so written in the source; the verse has أَنْ]. ﴿لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of علم, and the clause علم is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَتابَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَاقْرَؤُا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿تَيَسَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿عَلِمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿إِنَّ﴾ lightened from the heavy, and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter [Translator's note: again written إنّ in the source; the verse has أَنْ]. ﴿سَيَكُونُ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the fronted khabar of يكون; and ﴿مَرْضى﴾ its postponed noun; the clause is the khabar of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of علم, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَآخَرُونَ﴾ conjoined to مرضى. ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَآخَرُونَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ conjoined to «آخرون يضربون في الأرض». ﴿فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿قَرْضاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and ﴿حَسَناً﴾ an adjective. The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿وَما﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; and ﴿لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿مِنْ خَيْرٍ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿تَجِدُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to the Name of Majesty; and ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and ﴿خَيْراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَعْظَمَ﴾ conjoined to خيرا; and ﴿أَجْراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.
Sūrat al-Muddaththir (سورة المدّثر)
[

dervis-irab:15-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَبِيلًا): heavy, severe; from their saying كلأ وبيل وضم, i.e. pasture that is not found wholesome because of its heaviness. الوبيل is the thick staff, and from it comes الوابل for heavy rain. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «وبلت السماء وبلًا (of the pattern وعد) and وبولًا: its rain became heavy. The original was "وبل مطر السماء", and it was omitted because it is known; for this reason rain is called وابل. And الوبيل is الوضيم [Translator's note: so in the source; the word appears to be corrupt — the lexicons have الوخيم, "unwholesome"], و معنى». [Translator's note: the end of the quotation («وو معنى») appears corrupt in the source and is reproduced as it stands.]

* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شاهِداً عَلَيْكُمْ كَما أَرْسَلْنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا): a resumptive (mustaʾnaf) statement, brought to address the people of Mecca by way of iltifāt (shift of address) from the third person in His saying وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ and His saying وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ. إنّ and its noun; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar (predicate); إليكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أرسلنا; رسولا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); شاهدا is a naʿt (adjective) of رسولا; عليكم is attached to شاهدا. كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a sending like Our sending a messenger to Pharaoh"; ما is maṣdariyya, and the clause أرسلنا has no grammatical position; إلى فرعون is attached to أرسلنا, and رسولا is a direct object. Moses and Pharaoh were singled out for mention only because the reports about them were widespread in Mecca.
(فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْناهُ أَخْذاً وَبِيلًا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; عصى فرعون الرسول is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its direct object. الرسول was made definite only because when an indefinite noun is repeated it is repeated definite with the lām of prior reference (al-ʿahdiyya). When the Arabs mention a noun first and then speak of it a second time, they bring it definite with al-, or bring its pronoun, so that it is not confused with another, e.g. رأيت رجلا فأكرمت الرجل ("I saw a man and honoured the man"); had you said فأكرمت رجلا, one would imagine that he was other than the first. The full treatment of this will come at His saying إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْراً and his saying ﷺ: "One hardship will not overcome two eases." Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «He repeated it with alif and lām only so that it would be known that it is the first, as though He said: so Pharaoh disobeyed him». فأخذناه is conjoined to فعصى; it is a past verb, its agent and its direct object; أخذا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and وبيلا is an adjective.
(فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدانَ شِيباً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); تتقون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the agent. إن is conditional; كفرتم is a past verb and its agent, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then how will you guard yourselves". يوما is the object of تتقون, i.e. "how will you guard yourselves against the Day of Resurrection and its terror if you remain in disbelief and do not believe and do righteous deeds". It may also be an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "how can you have taqwā on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieve" — so said al-Zamakhsharī. Al-Samīn refuted him, saying it cannot be accusative as an adverb, because they will not disbelieve on that Day; rather they will inevitably believe on it. It may also be accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "if you disbelieve in the Day of Resurrection". The clause يجعل is an adjective of يوما; الولدان is the first direct object and شيبا the second direct object. More on the meaning of this description will come in the Rhetoric section.
(السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا): the clause is a second adjective of يوما. السماء is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and منفطر به is the khabar. Someone may ask why the adjective was not made feminine, so that منفطرة would be said. Several answers are given. Among them: that this form is a form of relation (nisba), i.e. "possessing splitting", as in امرأة مرضع and حائض, i.e. possessing nursing and possessing menstruation. Among them: that it was not made feminine because السماء has the meaning of "the roof"; the Exalted said: وَجَعَلْنَا السَّماءَ سَقْفاً مَحْفُوظاً. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It too describes the Day by its severity: that the heaven, despite its vastness and firmness, splits on it — so what do you think of other created things? The meaning is "possessing splitting", or it is by interpreting السماء as the roof. And the bāʾ in به is like that in your saying: فطرت العود بالقدوم فانفطر به (I split the wood with the adze and it split by it)». So on al-Zamakhsharī's view it is the bāʾ of instrument (istiʿāna); it has also been said to be causal; and al-Qurṭubī said it means "in" (fī). All amount to the same.
كان is a deficient (nāqiṣ) past verb; وعده is its noun and مفعولا its khabar. الوعد is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, so the pronoun in به refers to Allah the Exalted. It may also refer to the Day, in which case الوعد is a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. "the promise of the Day of Resurrection", and the agent is omitted.
(إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا): إنّ and its noun — the demonstrative points to the verses that speak of the promise and the threat — and تذكرة is its khabar. The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; شاء is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the object of شاء is omitted, its implied form being "whoever wills salvation". اتخذ is a past verb in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. إلى ربه is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of سبيلا, and سبيلا is the object of اتخذ.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ): a resumptive clause brought to clarify what was stated summarily at the beginning of the sūra. إنّ and its noun; the clause يعلم is its khabar; أنّ and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يعلم. The kāf is the noun of أنّ, and the clause تقوم is the khabar of أنك. أدنى is an adverb of time, i.e. "a time less than"; من ثلثي الليل is attached to أدنى. الأدنى, which means "the nearer", was borrowed for "the less" only because when the distance between two things is near, the space between them is little, and when it is far, that space is much.
(وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ): al-Zamakhsharī clarified this i'rab by saying: «It was read ونصفَه وثلثَه in the accusative, meaning that you stand less than two-thirds, and you stand the half and the third. This matches what came at the beginning of the sūra: the choice between standing the whole half, standing less than it — the third — and standing more than it — less than two-thirds. And it was read ونصفِه وثلثِه in the genitive, i.e. you stand less than two-thirds, and less than the half and the third. This matches the choice between the half, which is less than two-thirds, the third, which is less than the half, and the quarter, which is less than the third; and this is the last option».
(وَطائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ): the wāw is a conjunction; طائفة is conjoined to the pronoun of تقوم, which is permitted without an emphasizing pronoun because of the separation. A group of his Companions also stood, following his example. Among them were some who did not know how much of the night they had prayed and how much remained, so they would stand the whole night as a precaution; they stood until their feet swelled, for a year or more, and then Allah lightened it for them. من الذين is an adjective of طائفة, and معك is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يقدّر الليل والنهار is the khabar.
(عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ): علم is a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو. أن is lightened from the heavy (أنّ); its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause لن تحصوه is its khabar; أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of علم. As for the pronoun in تحصوه, al-Zamakhsharī said: «The maṣdar is implied, i.e. He knew that it is not feasible for you to fix the times precisely, nor is it possible to reckon them with exactness and evenness unless you take the broader course as a precaution, and that is hard and exhausting for you». This is better than the statement of al-Jalāl and others that it refers to the night because it is what was spoken of at the beginning of the sūra, even though the meaning is the same. فتاب is conjoined to علم, and عليكم is attached to تاب. The fāʾ is a conjunction; اقرءوا is an imperative verb and its agent; ما is a direct object; the clause تيسر is the ṣila; and من القرآن is attached to it.
(عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضى وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is resumptive. أن is lightened from the heavy, i.e. أنّه, and the clause سيكون is its khabar; منكم is the fronted khabar of يكون and مرضى its postponed noun. آخرون is a mubtadaʾ, منكم is a ḥāl, and the clause يضربون في الأرض is the khabar, i.e. they travel.
(يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَآخَرُونَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the clause يبتغون is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from the pronoun in يضربون; من فضل الله is attached to يبتغون. آخرون is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يقاتلون في سبيل الله is the khabar. For these three groups the night-standing mentioned is burdensome.
(فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; اقرءوا is an imperative verb and its agent; ما is a direct object; the clause تيسر is the ṣila; منه is attached to تيسر. أقيموا الصلاة is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and آتوا الزكاة is conjoined to أقيموا الصلاة.
(وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً وَما تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْراً): أقرضوا الله is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; قرضا is an absolute object and حسنا an adjective. The wāw is a conjunction.
ما is conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted object of تقدموا; تقدموا is the protasis; لأنفسكم is attached to تقدموا; من خير is a ḥāl; تجدوه is the apodosis; عند الله is an adverb of تجدوه. هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun. Abū al-Baqāʾ erred in allowing it to be a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ; had it been a substitute it would have matched it in the accusative, and would have been إيّاه. خيرا is the second object of تجدوه; أعظم is conjoined to خيرا, and أجرا is a tamyīz (specification). It is permitted for هو to be a pronoun of separation even though it does not come between two definite nouns, because it comes between a definite and an indefinite noun, but the indefinite resembles the definite in that it cannot take the definite article. The reason it cannot take the article is that it is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl), and al- may not enter it when من is with it, overtly or implicitly; here من is implied, i.e. "better than what you left behind".
(وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what precedes. إنّ and its noun and its two khabars form a nominal clause giving the reason for seeking forgiveness, i.e. seek His forgiveness in all your states, for man is exposed to shortcoming.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا» there is a predicative metaphor (majāz isnādī), a kināya (metonymy) for the intensity of the terror. Of a severe day it is said: "a day that whitens the forelocks of children". Its origin is that when cares and sorrows mount up in a person and take hold of him, grey hair comes upon him quickly. Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] clung to the fringes of this metaphor and said:
والهمّ يخترم الجسيم نحافة ... ويشيب ناصية الصبي ويهرم
(Care wastes away the stout body to leanness, and greys the forelock of the boy and makes him old.)

* Benefits:
Abū al-Samāʾil and Ibn al-Samayqaʿ read: هو خيرٌ, with both in the nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar. Abū Zayd said this is the dialect of Banū Tamīm: they put what follows the pronoun of separation in the nominative, saying كان زيد هو العاقلُ in the nominative. Thus this verse, by Qays ibn Dharīḥ:
تحنّ إلى ليلى وأنت تركتها ... وكنت عليها بالملا أنت أقدر
(You yearn for Laylā though you left her, and you were, over her, in the open plain, the more able.)
Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī said: Sībawayh recited this verse as evidence for the nominative, and the rhymes are nominative. I say: by this one may account for the verse of Abū Nuwās, in which some claimed he made a grammatical error:
دع عنك لومي فإن اللوم إغراء ... وداوني بالتي كانت هي الداء
(Leave off blaming me, for blame is incitement, and cure me with that which was itself the disease.)

dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُزَّمِّلُ) al-mutazammil, i.e. the one who has wrapped himself (tazammala) in his garments, i.e. wound them around himself, with the tāʾ assimilated into the zāy; similar to it is al-muddaththir from al-mutadaththir. One says تزمّل في ثوبه: he wrapped himself up; and زمّل: he wrapped. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
كأن ثبيرا في عرانين وبله ... كبير أناس في بجاد مزمل
(As though Thabīr, under the first of its downpour, were a chief of people wrapped in a striped cloak.)
And Dhū al-Rumma said:
وكائن تخطّت ناقتي من مفازة ... ومن نائم عن ليلها متزمل
(How many a desert has my she-camel crossed, and [passed] how many a sleeper, wrapped up, heedless of its night!)
In al-Miṣbāḥ: «زمّلته بثوبه تزميلا فتزمّل, like لففته فتلفّف ("I wrapped him and he became wrapped"). زملت الشيء: I carried the thing; from it the camel is called zāmila, with the hāʾ for intensification, because it carries the traveller's goods». More of its meaning will come in the section on benefits.
(ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ) rising after sleep. It is an adjective of something omitted, i.e. the soul that rises (al-nāshiʾa) at night, which rises from its bed for worship, i.e. lifts up and gets up; from نشأت السحابة when the cloud rose. It is also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning rising, from نشأ when he rose and got up, so it would be like al-ʿāqiba. In al-Mukhtār: «ناشئة الليل is its first hours; and it is said: the acts of obedience that arise in it».
(وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ) devote yourself exclusively to Him. تبتيلا is a maṣdar not of the [verb's own] maṣdar pattern, occurring in place of تبتّل, because the maṣdar of tafaʿʿala is tafaʿʿul, as in تصرّف تصرّفا and تكرّم تكرّما, whereas التبتيل is the maṣdar of بتّل, as in صرّف تصريفا. [Ibn Mālik] said in al-Khulāṣa:
وغير ذي ثلاثة مقيس ... مصدره كقدس التقديس
(The maṣdar of a verb of more than three letters is regular, as قدّس: التقديس.)
He said in al-Kashshāf: «If you say: How was تبتيلا said in place of تبتّلا? I say:
Because the meaning of تبتّل is "detach your soul (battil nafsaka)", so it was brought according to its meaning, in consideration of the right of the verse-endings». The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «His words, the Exalted, تبتيلا: a maṣdar not of the [verb's own] maṣdar, occurring in place of تبتّل; and it is said the meaning is: detach yourself completely».
(النَّعْمَةِ) with fatḥa: living in ease; with kasra: bestowing favour; with ḍamma: joy.
(أَنْكالًا) heavy fetters; plural of nikl, with kasra on the nūn.
(كَثِيباً) heaped-up sand.
(مَهِيلًا) flowing after having been heaped up. It is from هال يهيل, and it is a passive participle whose origin is mahyūl: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was moved to the hāʾ; the wāw, the second of two quiescent letters, was dropped because it is the additional one; and the ḍamma was changed to a kasra to suit the yāʾ. In al-Mukhtār: «هال الدقيق في الجراب: he poured the flour into the bag without measuring; anything that one lets go freely, of sand, dust, food and the like, one has هاله, so it انهار, i.e. ran and poured down; its pattern is باع; أهال is a dialectal form of it, so it is مُهال and مَهيل».

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) يا is a vocative particle, and أيّها is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is an intended indefinite noun, and the hāʾ is for alerting; المزمل is a badal (substitute) or an adjective (naʿt). قم is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; الليل is an adverb of قم, even if the action occurring in it covers it entirely. إلا is a particle of exception and قليلا is excepted from الليل; in this is evidence that the excepted may be of vague quantity. (نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا) The grammarians permitted نصفه to be a badal from الليل or from قليلا. If it is a badal from الليل, the exception is from it, and what he is commanded to stand in prayer is half the night except a little of it, and the pronoun in منه and عليه refers to the half. The meaning then becomes: stand half the night except a little, or reduce half the night a little, or add to half the night; so His words "or reduce half the night a little" would be a repetition of His words "except a little of half the night", and that is an ineloquent construction from which the Qur'an is to be kept free. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «نصفه is a badal from الليل, and إلا قليلا is an exception from the half, as though He said: stand less than half. The pronoun in منه and عليه is for the half. The meaning is a choice between two things: between standing less than half the night decisively, and choosing one of two things, namely reducing from the half and adding to it». Abū Ḥayyān said, commenting on al-Zamakhsharī's i'rab: «He did not notice the repetition that this view entails, because on his estimation, "stand less than half the night", "or reduce from half the night" would be a repetition. And if نصفه is a badal from His words إلا قليلا, then the pronoun in نصفه either refers to the thing substituted for, or to the thing excepted from, which is الليل. It cannot refer to the thing substituted for, because it would become an exception of an unknown from an unknown, since the implied form would be "except a little, half of the little", and this has no valid meaning at all. If the pronoun refers to الليل, there is no benefit in excepting from the night, since it would have been shorter, clearer and further from ambiguity for the construction to be قم الليل نصفه. We have refuted the view of whoever said that إلا قليلا is an exception from the badal, which is نصفه, and that the implied form is "stand half the night except a little of it", i.e. of the half. Moreover, the claim that نصفه is a badal from إلا قليلا and that the pronoun in نصفه refers to الليل involves applying "little" to the half; and it also entails that the implied form becomes: except half of it, so do not stand it; or reduce from the half that you do not stand; or add to it the half that you do not stand — and this is a meaning that is not sound and is definitely not what is meant by the verse». Al-Zamakhsharī also said: «If you wish, you may make نصفه a badal from قليلا, and it would be a choice among three: between standing the whole half, standing less than it, and standing more than it. The half is described as little only in relation to the whole. And if you wish, you may say: since the meaning of قم الليل إلا قليلا نصفه, when you make the half a badal from الليل, is "stand less than half the night", the pronoun in منه and عليه refers to the "less than half"; so it is as though it were said: stand less than half the night, and stand less than that "less", or more than it, a little; so the choice beyond the half is between it and the third. It is also permissible, when you make نصفه a badal from قليلا and explain it by it, to make the second قليلا mean half of the half, which is the quarter, as though it were said: or reduce from it a little, half of it; and to make what is added to this "little" — I mean the quarter — half of the quarter, as though it were said: or add to it a little, half of it. You may also make the addition, because it is unrestricted, the completion of the third, so it would be a choice among the half, the third and the quarter». Abū Ḥayyān followed him up, as is his habit, and said: «How wide is this man's imagination! He permits what is near and what is far, while the Qur'an may only be construed according to the best of the ways that occur in the speech of the Arabs». Among those who stated explicitly that نصفه may be a badal from الليل or from قليلا are al-Zamakhsharī, as we have reported from him; Ibn ʿAṭiyya, who presented it as a possibility; and Abū al-Baqāʾ, who said: «It is more in keeping with the apparent sense of the verse that it be a badal from قليلا, أو زد عليه [Translator's note: the source seems to have dropped words here, e.g. "because of His words أو انقص منه … أو زد عليه"], the hāʾ in both being for the half; for if the exception were from the half, the implied form would become "stand half the night except a little, or reduce from it a little", and the excepted "little" is not determined, so reducing from it cannot be realised». As for al-Khawfī [Translator's note: so in the source; probably al-Ḥawfī], he permitted it to be a badal from الليل and mentioned nothing else.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In my view His words إلا قليلا may possibly be an exception from the standing, with الليل made a generic noun». Then he said: «إلا قليلا, i.e. the nights in which you fail to stand because of a clear excuse; this view is good with the opinion that it is recommended [rather than obligatory]». Abū Ḥayyān said in comment: «This is contrary to the apparent sense. It is said that the meaning is "or half of it", as you say "give him a dirham, two dirhams, three", meaning "or two dirhams or three"; this involves omitting the conjunction without any indication of it». Or [as] al-Tibrīzī said: «The command to stand and the choice of adding and reducing fall on the last two thirds of the night, because the first third is the time of the night prayer (al-ʿatama), and the exception applies to what is commanded. It is as though He said: stand the night except a little; then He made نصفه a badal from قليلا, so the "little" is explained as half of the two thirds, which is little in relation to the whole. So His words أو انقص منه, i.e. from what is commanded, which is standing the third [Translator's note: so in the source], قليلا, i.e. less than half of it, أو زد عليه, i.e. over the two thirds; so the choice of adding and reducing falls on the two thirds». [Translator's note: the quotation is not closed in the source; it is assumed to end here.] (أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا) Aw is a conjunction of choice, i.e. among standing half the night, more than it up to two thirds, and less than it down to a third. زد is an imperative verb and عليه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) زد. رتل القرآن is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ترتيلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا) The clause is a parenthesis between the command to stand at night and its justification by His coming words إن ناشئة الليل etc.; it is also said that it is resumptive. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «This verse is a parenthesis. By the heavy word He means the Qur'an and the commands and prohibitions in it, which are hard, heavy obligations on those charged with them, and especially on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because he bears them himself and lays them on his community, so they are heavier for him and more burdensome to him. By this parenthesis He meant that the standing at night with which He charged him is among the heavy, difficult obligations that the Qur'an came with, because the night is the time of sleep, rest and stillness, so whoever keeps it alive must go against his nature and struggle with his soul». Inna and its noun, and the clause سنلقي is its khabar (predicate); عليك is attached to نلقي; قولا is the direct object and ثقيلا an adjective, i.e. a great, majestic, awe-inspiring speech of weight; everything that has weight and worth is heavy. (إِنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا) The clause gives the reason for what preceded. Inna and its noun; هي is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ (subject); أشد is the khabar of inna, or the khabar of هي with the clause being the khabar of inna; وطئا is a tamyīz (specification); أقوم is conjoined to أشد, and قيلا is a tamyīz, i.e. speech. (إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهارِ سَبْحاً طَوِيلًا) Inna is a particle resembling the verb, and لك is the fronted khabar of inna; في النهار is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of سبحا; سبحا is the noun of inna, and طويلا is its delayed noun [Translator's note: so in the source; طويلا is evidently an adjective of سبحا]. The meaning of al-sabḥ will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا) conjoined to what preceded; اسم ربك is the object of اذكر, i.e. persist in it night and day, in whatever state and manner. تبتل is an imperative verb and إليه is attached to it; تبتيلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا) رب المشرق is read in the nominative, so it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and it is read in the genitive as a badal from ربك; both readings are among the seven. The i'rab of the testimony لا إله إلا هو has preceded in al-Baqara. The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ, i.e. if you have known that and believed in it, then take Him. اتخذه is an imperative verb, a latent agent and the first direct object, and وكيلا is the second direct object. (وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْراً جَمِيلًا) conjoined to what preceded. اصبر is an imperative verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa" [Translator's note: so in the source; with an imperative addressed to the Prophet the implied form is "anta"]; على ما is attached to اصبر, and the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; اهجرهم is conjoined to اصبر; هجرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and جميلا an adjective. (وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا) also conjoined. ذرني is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; المكذبين is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the direct object. The meaning is: I will suffice you against them, so do not grieve or be sad. أولي النعمة is an adjective of المكذبين. مهّلهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; قليلا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or an adverb, i.e. a little time. (إِنَّ لَدَيْنا أَنْكالًا وَجَحِيماً) Inna is a particle resembling the verb; لدينا is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is its fronted khabar; أنكالا is its delayed noun, and جحيما is conjoined to أنكالا. (وَطَعاماً ذا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذاباً أَلِيماً) conjoined to أنكالا; ذا غصة is an adjective; it is the zaqqūm or the ḍarīʿ, on which one chokes in the throat.
عذابا is also conjoined. (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبالُ وَكانَتِ الْجِبالُ كَثِيباً مَهِيلًا) The adverb is attached to the [notion of] being settled to which لدينا is attached; you may also attach it to an omitted element that is an adjective of عذابا, i.e. a punishment befalling on the day the earth quakes. The clause ترجف الأرض is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it. The wāw is a conjunction; كانت الجبال is kāna and its noun; كثيبا is its khabar and مهيلا an adjective of كثيبا.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the preceding verses the antithesis (ṭibāq) between المشرق and المغرب appears clearly.
2- In His words «إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya). Al-sabḥ is the maṣdar of سبح; it is borrowed from swimming in water for moving about in the ways of livelihood and in people's needs, i.e. you have in the daytime moving about and turning to and fro in important affairs, as the swimmer goes back and forth in the water. The poet said:
أباحوا لكم شرق البلاد وغربها ... ففيها لكم يا صاح سبح من السبح
(They have opened to you the east of the land and its west; so in it, my friend, you have ample room to range about.)
It was also read سبخا, with the dotted khāʾ, and its meaning is lightness from obligations; al-tasbīkh is lightening. It is a metaphor from سبخ الصوف when one fluffs up wool and spreads its parts; its meaning is the scattering of concern and the dispersal of thought among preoccupations. Pieces of cotton are called sabāʾikh, singular sabīkha; from it is the saying of al-Akhṭal:
فأرسلوهنّ يذرين التراب كما ... يذري سبائخ قطن ندف أوتار
(They let them loose, scattering the dust as the bow-strings of carding scatter tufts of cotton.)

* Benefits:
The sayings of the exegetes on this address differed, in three views:
1- ʿIkrima said: O you who are wrapped in prophethood and cloaked in the message. Also from him: O you who wrapped up this matter, i.e. bore it, then slackened.
2- Ibn ʿAbbās said: O you who are wrapped in the Qur'an.
3- Qatāda said: O you who are wrapped in his garments. This was at the beginning of the revelation to him, for when the revelation came to him ﷺ in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, he returned to Khadīja, his wife, with his heart trembling, and said: "Wrap me up, wrap me up! I feared for myself that this might be the beginnings of poetry or soothsaying" — all of that being from the devil — "and that the one who appeared with the revelation was not the angel". Khadīja, who was a truthful helper, said to him: "No, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you: you maintain ties of kinship, you host the guest and you help in the calamities of truth".
It is also said that he ﷺ was sleeping at night, wrapped in a velvet blanket, and was called with what disparages that state he was in of being wrapped in his blanket. Al-Zamakhsharī clung to this opinion and expressed it in a phrasing eloquent in itself, but he offended against the Messenger ﷺ. We quote below his wording and Ibn al-Munayyir's comment on it, because of their interest and because they are of high literary quality:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sleeping at night, wrapped in his velvet blanket, and was called with what disparages to him the state he was in of being wrapped in his blanket and his readiness to sink into heavy sleep, as one does who is not concerned by any matter and not occupied by any affair. Do you not see the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
وكائن تخطّت ناقتي من مفازة ... ومن نائم عن ليلها متزمّل
(How many a desert has my she-camel crossed, and [passed] how many a sleeper, wrapped up, heedless of its night!)
He means the lazy, sluggish one who does not rise to great matters and the burdens of affairs, and does not bear hardships and toils. Similar to it is:
فأتت به حوش الفؤاد مبطنا ... سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل
(She bore him keen of heart, lean of belly, wakeful when the night of the dullard sleeps.)
And in their proverbs:
أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل ... ما هكذا يا سعد تورد الإبل
(Saʿd brought them to water while Saʿd was wrapped in his cloak; not thus, O Saʿd, are camels brought to water.)
He censured him for wrapping himself in his cloak and made that the opposite of earnestness and shrewdness. And He commanded him to choose night vigil over sleep, and over being wrapped up, girding himself and lightening himself for worship and striving in Allah's cause. No wonder, then, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ girded himself for that, together with his Companions, with true girding; they devoted themselves to keeping their nights alive, rejected sleep and ease for it, and strove in it until their feet swelled, their colour turned pale and the mark appeared on their faces, and their situation reached a point where their Lord had mercy on them for it and lightened [the obligation] for them». By my life, al-Zamakhsharī was fair to the Prophet and his Companions and described their worship and the wearing-out of their souls in a manner befitting them; however, his first phrases are somewhat misleading, and for that reason Ibn al-Munayyir took him to task for them, saying: «As for his first saying, that calling him [thus] is a disparagement of the state he mentioned he was in, and his adducing the verses mentioned as evidence, it is an error and bad manners. Whoever considers the customary manner of Allah the Exalted's addressing him with honour and reverence will know the falsity of what al-Zamakhsharī imagined. The scholars have said that he was never addressed by his name in a vocative, and that this is one of his special features to the exclusion of the other messengers, out of honour and ennoblement for him. So how far is calling him with a disparaging form from calling him by his name! And [as for] his adducing as evidence for that verses said in censure of uncouth, barefoot herdsmen — I declare myself free before Allah of that, and I hold him ﷺ far above it». His saying «أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل» reminded me of what I came across of the words of Ibn Kharūf the grammarian, rebutting al-Zamakhsharī and faulting his opinion in his composition al-Mufaṣṣal and his excessive abridgement of the meanings of Sībawayh's words, so that Ibn Kharūf called it "al-Barnāmaj" (the programme/index) and recited about it:
أوردها سعد وسعد مشتمل ... ما هكذا يا سعد تورد الإبل
(Saʿd brought them to water while Saʿd was wrapped in his cloak; not thus, O Saʿd, are camels brought to water.)
I say: there is no avoiding saying that Ibn al-Munayyir was very unfair to al-Zamakhsharī and ignored the enjoyable, precise description he gave of his girding himself ﷺ and his worship; but citing verses said in censure in this connection is an error that al-Zamakhsharī fell into, and many an error arises from something correct. There is no harm, after this, in citing the wording of al-Suhaylī in this connection, for he reached the utmost in it in explanation, interpretation and subtlety of analysis. He said: «al-Muzzammil is not one of his names, upon him be blessing and peace, by which he is known; it is only derived from the state he was involved in at the time of the address. When the Arabs intend gentleness towards the one addressed and to leave off reproach, they call him by a name derived from the state he is in, as the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, when he had slept and dust had stuck to his side: "Get up, Abū Turāb", indicating that he was being gentle with him. So His words يا أيها المزمّل contain friendliness and gentleness».

farraa:1-3.t:
The readers are agreed on doubling in المُزَّمِّل and المُدَّثِّر. المزمّل is the one who has wrapped himself in his garments and made ready for prayer, and he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُمِ ٱلْلَّيْلَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
He means: the last third. Then He said: ﴿نِّصْفَهُ﴾.
The meaning is: or half of it. Then He granted him a dispensation and said: ﴿أَوِ ٱنقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً﴾ — from the half down to the third — or add to the half up to two thirds. This was before the five prayers were made obligatory; when the prayer was made obligatory, it abrogated this, just as zakat abrogated every [other obligatory] charity and the month of Ramadan every [other obligatory] fast.

farraa:14-14.t:
﴿وَكَانَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَثِيباً مَّهِيلاً﴾.
الكثيب is sand, and المهيل is that whose bottom is disturbed so that it pours down on you from its top. المهيل is the passive participle; the Arabs say: مهيل and مهيول, مكيد and مكيود. The poet said:
وناهزُوا البيعَ من تِرْعِيَّةٍ رَهِقٍ * مُستَأْرَبٍ، عَضَّه السُّلطانُ مَديُونُ
(They hastened to the sale from a herdsman, burdened, deep in debt, whom the authority has bitten — indebted.)
He said: al-Farrāʾ said: المستأرَب is one who has been seized by his limbs [i.e. utterly], and [one says] قد أُرِّب.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْماً﴾.
Its meaning is: how will you guard yourselves against a day that will turn children grey, if you disbelieve? And it is exactly so in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾.
[I.e.] by that day. السماء is treated as masculine and feminine; here it is treated as masculine. The poet said:
فلو رَفع السماءُ إليه قوماً * لحقنا بالنجومِ مع السحابِ
(If the sky had raised a people up to it, we would have joined the stars along with the clouds.)

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
A path and a direction to Allah.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَيِ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with the accusative, and the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī with the genitive. Whoever uses the genitive means: you stand less than two thirds, and less than half, and [less] than a third. Whoever uses the accusative means: you stand less than two thirds, standing half or a third; and this is closer to being right, because He said "less than two thirds" and then mentioned the explanation of the "less", not the explanation of something less than the "less". Do you not see that you say to a man: لى عليك أقل من ألف درهم ثمانى مائة أو تسع مائة (you owe me less than a thousand dirhams: eight hundred or nine hundred)? That is, as it were, sounder in meaning than explaining another "less" [111/b]; and both are correct.
﴿وَطَآئِفَةٌ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَ﴾: the Prophet ﷺ and a group of the Muslims used to stand [in prayer] at night before the prayer was made obligatory; that was hard on them, so the dispensation came down. It would also be permissible to put النصف in the genitive and الثلث in the accusative, according to the interpretation of some that the Prophet's ﷺ prayer extended to a third of the night; so they said: your Lord knows that you stand less than two thirds and [less] than half, and you do not fall short of a third. But this is an anomalous way (shādhdh) which no one has read. The people of recitation who are followed know the interpretation better than the newcomers. It is [nevertheless] permissible, and in my view it means: the third.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ﴾: that you will not keep track of the times of the night. ﴿فَٱقْرَءُواْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ﴾: a hundred [verses] or more. They have mentioned that whoever recites ten verses is not recorded among the heedless. And every [part] of the night that one who prays keeps alive [in prayer] is ناشئة.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾: He means the obligatory [prayer].

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلاً﴾.
He is saying: recite it at your ease, unhurriedly.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلاً ثَقِيلاً﴾.
That is: not light or trivial, because it is the speech of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ ٱللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْأً﴾.
He is saying: it is firmer in standing. ﴿وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلاً﴾: He is saying: in the day people are restless and move about for their livelihood, while the night is freer for the heart; so He made it more upright in speech.
Some said: the rising by night is harder on the one who prays than the day prayer, because the night is for sleep; so He said: it, even though it is harder in treading, is more upright in speech. The readers are agreed on fatḥa on the wāw of وطئاً. Some read: "هى أشَدُّ وطئاً" — he said: al-Farrāʾ said: write وطئا without alif — [and some read: هى أشد وِطَاء], with kasra on the wāw and lengthening, meaning: harder in toil, labour and conformity (muwāṭaʾa). As for الوِطء — we have not transmitted وِطء from any of the readers.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ سَبْحَاً طَوِيلاً﴾.
He is saying: you have in the daytime [time] in which to see to your needs. Some read: "سبخا" with khāʾ; التسبيخ is the loosening of wool, cotton and the like; one says: سبِّخى قطنك (fluff out your cotton). Abū al-Faḍl said: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh say: Abū Ziyād al-Kilābī attended al-Farrāʾ's session on that day, and al-Farrāʾ asked him about this word, and he said: The people of our desert say: اللهم سبِّخ عنه (O Allah, lighten [it] from him), for the sick person, the one stung [by a scorpion] and the like.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلاً﴾.
Devote yourself sincerely to Allah. It is said of a worshipper, when he leaves everything and turns to worship: قد تبتل, i.e. he has cut himself off from everything except the command of Allah and obedience to Him.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَّبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it in the genitive, and the people of the Ḥijāz in the nominative. The nominative is good when one verse is separated from another. Similar to it: ﴿وتَذَرُونَ أحْسَنَ الْخَالِقِينَ، اللهُ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ [111/a]: in these two places both starting afresh (istiʾnāf) and making it follow (itbāʿ) are good.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلاً﴾.
[I.e.] a guarantor of what He has promised you.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «الليل» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قم»; «قليلا» is an excepted [noun], accusative (manṣūb).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «نصفه» is a badal (substitute) from {اللَّيْلَ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «منه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «انقص»; «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a little decrease.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «قولا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «إنَّا سنلقي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «هي أشد» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; «وطئا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في النهار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «واذكر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «رتل» in verse (4); «تبتيلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar (verbal noun) being التبتُّل.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «رب» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: He is the Lord (هو رب), and the clause «هو رب» is resumptive; the clause of transcendence [«لا إله إلا هو»] is a second khabar of the implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ «هو»; the clause «فاتخذه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause of transcendence; «وكيلا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «ما» is a nominal relative in the position of a genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصبر».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: His words «والمكذبين»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ in «ذرني»; «أولي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «المكذبين», genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; it is inflexible (jāmid) but interpreted as a derived word (أصحاب, possessors); «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the adverb «لدينا» is attached; the clause «وكانت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ترجف», in the position of a genitive; «مهيلا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيبا».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «شاهدا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «عليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شاهدا»; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a sending like Our sending, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival); «رسولا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «فعصى فرعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {أَرْسَلْنَا}, and the clause «فأخذناه» is conjoined to the clause «عصى».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تتقون»; the clause «تتقون» is resumptive; the clause «إن كفرتم» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it; «يوما» is the object of «تتقون»; the clause «يجعل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوما»; «شيبا» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «السماء منفطر به» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {يَوْمًا}; the attribute comes in the masculine because «السماء» may be treated as masculine or feminine; the clause «كان وعده مفعولا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «إن هذه تذكرة»; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «إلى ربه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اتخذ».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «أنَّ» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «يعلم»; «أدنى» is an adverb of time, i.e.: a time less; the preposition and its genitive noun «من ثلثي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أدنى»; «ونصفه» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أدنى». His words «وطائفة»: a noun conjoined to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «تقوم»; this conjunction is permitted because of a separating element between them; the clause «والله يقدر» is conjoined to the clause «إن ربك يعلم»; the clause «علم» is resumptive; «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy [أنَّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن تحصوه» is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened «أن», and «أن» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the clause «فتاب» is conjoined to «علم». The clause «فاقرءوا» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من القرآن» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما»; the clause «علم أن سيكون» is resumptive; «مرضى» is the noun of «يكون»; the preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to the khabar. His words «وآخرون»: a noun conjoined to «مرضى»; the clause «يضربون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آخرون», and the clause «يبتغون» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يضربون». His words «وآخرون يقاتلون»: a noun conjoined to the previous «آخرون», and the clause «يقاتلون» is a naʿt; the clause «فاقرءوا» is resumptive; «قرضا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). His words «وما»: the wāw is parenthetical, and «ما» is a conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun «من خير» is attached to an omitted naʿt of «ما»; «هو» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «تجدوه»; «خيرا» is the second object of «تجدوه»; the clause «وما تقدِّموا» is parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses; and the clause «استغفروا» is conjoined to the clause «أقرضوا».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (يا أيها المزمل): the origin of (المزمل) is (المتزمل); then the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (نصفه): a badal (substitute) from (الليل). It is also said that it is accusative with an implied "Stand half of it". Both are adverbials of time.
His saying (وطأ): whoever reads it with fatḥa on the wāw makes it accusative as an explanation (bayān), and whoever reads it with kasra and a long vowel makes it accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying (كثيبا): the khabar (predicate) of (كان), and (مهيلا) is its naʿt (adjective). The origin of (مهيلا) is (مهيول); it is the passive participle mafʿūl from (هلت). The vowel of the yāʾ was thrown onto the hāʾ, so two vowelless letters met, and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of the two vowelless letters; the hāʾ was given kasra so that the yāʾ after it would remain sound; so the measure of its wording is mafīl (مفيل) [Translator's note: the printed text has «مقيل»]. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said that it is the yāʾ that was dropped, and that the wāw indicates a meaning, so it is the one remaining. They should then have said (مهول), except that they said the hāʾ was given kasra before the yāʾ was dropped because of its proximity to the yāʾ; then when the yāʾ was dropped, the wāw turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. So the yāʾ in (مهيلا) is, on their view, augmentative, and on the first view it is radical. All of them allowed it to come in its original form in speech, so you say (مهيول), and likewise (مبيوع) and the like among verbs with yāʾ as a radical. If it is from those with wāw, it may not come in its original form according to the Basrans, while the Kufans allowed it, as in (مقوول) and (مصووغ). All of them allowed (مبوع) and (مهول) according to the dialect of those who say (بوع المتاع) and (قول القول), which is the dialect of Hudhayl; and the disagreement about what is dropped in it is as stated above.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (رب المشرق): whoever reads it in the nominative takes it as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (لا إله إلا هو) is the khabar (predicate); it may also have an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Lord of the East". Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a badal (substitute) from (ربك) or a naʿt (adjective) of it.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (وذرني والمكذبين): (المكذبين) is conjoined to the nūn and yāʾ, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
His saying (ومهلهم قليلا): (قليلا) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverbial.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (يوم ترجف): the governor of (يوم) is the notion of being settled (al-istiqrār) indicated by (لدينا), just as you say "Zayd is behind you today" (إن خلفك زيدا اليوم): the governor of (اليوم) is the istiqrār indicated by (خلفك), and it is also the governor of (خلفك). It may govern two adverbials because they differ, one being an adverbial of place and the other an adverbial of time; as if you had said "Zayd is settled behind you today". Likewise the verse: its implied form is "Shackles and a blazing fire are settled with Us on the day the earth quakes."

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (كما أرسلنا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (رسول) or of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (يوما يجعل): (يوم) is accusative governed by (تتقون); it is not an adverbial of (كفرتم) [Translator's note: the printed text has «لكفرتهم»], because they do not disbelieve on that day; unless you make (تكفرون) mean "deny", so that you make the day accusative by (تكفرون) as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverbial. (يجعل) is a naʿt (adjective) of (اليوم) if you make the pronoun in (يجعل) refer back to the day. If you make it refer back to Allah, exalted be His mention, it is not a naʿt of the day except with an implied hāʾ, the implied form being "a day in which Allah makes the children grey-headed", so it is a naʿt of the day because of the pronoun.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying (السماء منفطر به): (منفطر) came without hāʾ although (السماء) is feminine only because it has the meaning of attribution (nasab), i.e. "the sky, possessing a splitting by it". It is also said that it is masculine only because (السماء) means "the roof", and the roof is masculine. Al-Farrāʾ said: (السماء) is treated as both masculine and feminine, so (منفطر) came in the masculine.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying (ونصفه وثلثه): whoever reads them in the genitive conjoins them to (ثلثي الليل), i.e. "and less than half of it and a third of it"; whoever reads them in the accusative conjoins them to (أدنى), i.e. "and you stand half of it and a third of it".
His saying (علم أن لن تحصوه): if you make it mean "you will not preserve its measure", it indicates the strength [of the genitive reading] [Translator's note: the printed text reads «يدل على قوة الحفظ» "indicates the strength of preservation"; the sense of the argument seems to be the strength of the genitive (الخفض)], because if they do not count it precisely, it is undefined, so it is less than the half and less than the third, undefined. And if it is read in the accusative, it is defined, counted, not unknown. So the genitive is stronger in meaning because of His saying (أن لن تحصوه), unless you construe (تحصوه) in the sense of "you will not be able to bear it", in which case the two readings are equal in strength. Al-Farrāʾ allowed (نصفه) in the genitive, conjoined to (ثلثي), and (ثلثه) in the accusative, conjoined to (أدنى).
His saying (أن سيكون منكم مرضى): (أن) is lightened from the heavy one, and the hāʾ is implied; (سيكون) is the khabar (predicate), the sīn being a compensation for the doubling. (مرضى) is the noun of (كان) and (منكم) is the khabar. (سيكون) came in the masculine form because the femininity of (مرضى) is not real.
His saying (وآخرون): conjoined to (مرضى).
His saying (هو خيرا): accusative as the second object of (تجدوا), and (هو) is a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿أيها﴾: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda); and هـا is for drawing attention (tanbīh).
﴿المزمل﴾: an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿قم﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿الليل﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for ﴿قم﴾.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿قليلا﴾: excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿نصفه﴾: a badal (substitute) of الليل, or of ﴿قليلا﴾.
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿انقص﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿منه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انقص﴾.
﴿قليلا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿أو﴾: أو is a conjunction denoting choice (takhyīr).
﴿زد﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿زد﴾.
﴿ورتل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and رتل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿القرآن﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ترتيلا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿إنا﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿سنلقي﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future, and نلقي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied ḍamma because of heaviness; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿عليك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نلقي﴾.
﴿قولا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ثقيلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿ناشئة﴾: the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (manṣūb); and it is muḍāf.
﴿الليل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
﴿هي﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿أشد﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿وطئا﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative.
﴿وأقوم﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أشد.
﴿قيلا﴾: tamyīz, accusative.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿في النهار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿سبحا﴾, because it was originally an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿سبحا﴾.
﴿سبحا﴾: the postponed ism (noun) of inna.
﴿طويلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿واذكر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and اذكر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿اسم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); and it is muḍāf.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وتبتل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿إليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تبتل﴾.
﴿تبتيلا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because the maṣdar (verbal noun) (of this verb) is ﴿تبتُّلًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
