﴿رب﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "He is the Lord"; and it is muḍāf.
﴿المشرق﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
﴿والمغرب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and المغرب is conjoined (maʿṭūf), genitive by the kasra; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿ربك﴾.
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins).
﴿إله﴾: its ism (noun), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) of the position of لا with its ism, because their position is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or a badal of the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar. And the clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ.
﴿فاتخذه﴾: the fāʾ of eloquence (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); اتخذ is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وكيلا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿واصبر﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; اصبر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿على ما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿يقولون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿واهجرهم﴾: conjoined to what preceded; اهجر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿هجرا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿جميلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وذرني﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; ذر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿والمكذبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and المكذبين is conjoined, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ.
﴿أولي﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative by the yāʾ, because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; and it is muḍāf.
﴿النعمة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿ومهلهم﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿قليلا﴾: a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, or an adverb, i.e.: "a little while".

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿لدينا﴾: لدى is an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; and it is muḍāf, and ﴿نا﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أنكالا﴾: the postponed ism (noun) of inna.
﴿وجحيما﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أنكالا﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وطعاما﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أنكالا﴾, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ذا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿طعاما﴾, accusative by the alif, because it is one of the six nouns; and it is muḍāf.
﴿غصة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr).
﴿وعذابا﴾: conjoined to ﴿طعاما﴾, accusative.
﴿أليما﴾: a naʿt of ﴿عذابا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the (notion of) "being established" (al-istiqrār) to which ﴿لدينا﴾ is attached, or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذابا﴾; and it is muḍāf.
﴿ترجف﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿الأرض﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of ترجف, nominative.
﴿والجبال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الجبال is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الأرض.
﴿وكانت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; kāna is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿الجبال﴾: the ism (noun) of kāna, nominative.
﴿كثيبا﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿مهيلا﴾: a naʿt of ﴿كثيبا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنا﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿أرسلنا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the ﴿نا﴾ of the agents; and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾.
﴿رسولا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿شاهدا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رسولا﴾.
﴿عليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿شاهدا﴾.
﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an attribute (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar; and ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿أرسلنا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the ﴿نا﴾ of the agents; and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما أرسلنا﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إلى فرعون﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾.
﴿رسولا﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿فعصى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and عصى is a past verb.
﴿فرعون﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الرسول﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿فأخذناه﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فعصى﴾; it is a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أخذا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿وبيلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أخذا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فكيف﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and كيف is interrogative, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿تتقون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كفرتم﴾: a past verb, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the fāʿil.
﴿يوما﴾: the object of ﴿تتقون﴾, accusative (manṣūb); or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e.: "if you disbelieve in the Day of Resurrection".
﴿يجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو), referring to ﴿يوما﴾; and the clause يجعل is an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿يوما﴾.
﴿الولدان﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿شيبا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿السماء﴾: السماء is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿منفطر﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; and the clause is a second attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿يوما﴾.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿منفطر﴾; the bāʾ is for instrument (istiʿāna); it has also been said: causal; and it has been said: it means في ("in").
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.
﴿وعده﴾: the ism (noun) of kāna, nominative; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿مفعولا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿هذه﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the ism (noun) of inna.
﴿تذكرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿شاء﴾: شاء is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the object of شاء is omitted, its implied form being: "whoever wills salvation".
﴿اتخذ﴾: a past verb in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of ﴿من﴾.
﴿إلى ربه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿سبيلا﴾.
﴿سبيلا﴾: the object of ﴿اتخذ﴾, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ربك﴾: the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (manṣūb); رب is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يعلم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿أنك﴾: anna is an abrogating particle, and the kāf is its ism.
﴿تقوم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "you" (أنت); and the clause is the khabar of anna; and anna with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ﴿يعلم﴾.
﴿أدنى﴾: an adverb of time, accusative, i.e.: "a time less (than)".
﴿من﴾: a preposition.
﴿ثلثي﴾: a genitive noun, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is a dual; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدنى﴾; and أدنى is muḍāf. [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿ثلثي﴾ is the word in construct (with الليل), not أدنى.]
﴿الليل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
﴿ونصفه﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدنى, accusative; نصف is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وثلثه﴾: conjoined to ﴿أدنى﴾, accusative; ثلث is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وطائفة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and طائفة is conjoined to the pronoun of تقوم.
﴿من الذين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿طائفة﴾.
﴿معك﴾: مع: an adverb, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. مع is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative.
﴿يقدر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿الليل﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
﴿والنهار﴾: conjoined to الليل. And the clause ﴿والله يقدر...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿علم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿تحصوه﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of its subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿لن تحصوه...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن; and أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of علم.
﴿فتاب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and تاب is a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿عليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تاب﴾.
﴿فاقرءوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اقرءوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿تيسر﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "it" (هو); and the clause ﴿تَيَسَّر﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿من القرآن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تيسر﴾.
﴿علم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter.
﴿سيكون﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future, and يكون is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative; and the clause ﴿سيكون...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿منكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar of يكون.
﴿مرضى﴾: the postponed ism of يكون.
﴿وآخرون﴾: conjoined to مرضى, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿يضربون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of ﴿آخرون﴾.
﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يضربون﴾.
﴿يبتغون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in ﴿يبتغون﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source; the ḥāl is evidently from the wāw in ﴿يضربون﴾.]
﴿من فضل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبتغون﴾; and فضل is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
﴿وآخرون﴾: conjoined to مرضى, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿يقاتلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of ﴿آخرون﴾.
﴿في سبيل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يقاتلون﴾; and سبيل is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
﴿فاقرءوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and اقرءوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿ما﴾: a relative (noun), mafʿūl bihi.
﴿تيسر﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "it" (هو); and the clause ﴿تَيَسَّر﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿منه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تيسر﴾.
﴿وأقيموا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أقيموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿الصلاة﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿وآتوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause is conjoined to ﴿أقيموا الصلاة﴾.
﴿الزكاة﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿وأقرضوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أقرضوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿قرضا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar).
﴿حسنا﴾: a naʿt of ﴿قرضا﴾, accusative.
﴿وما﴾: conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of ﴿تقدموا﴾.
﴿تقدموا﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿لأنفسكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تقدموا﴾.
﴿من خير﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl.
﴿تجدوه﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿عند﴾: an adverb for ﴿تجدوه﴾, accusative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
﴿هو﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
﴿خيرا﴾: the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿تجدوه﴾.
﴿وأعظم﴾: conjoined to ﴿خيرا﴾, accusative.
﴿أجرا﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative.
﴿واستغفروا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and استغفروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, the ism of inna, accusative.
﴿غفور﴾: the khabar of inna, nominative.
﴿رحيم﴾: a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾, nominative; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original form is المتزمّل; the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy. There are three views on its meaning. The view of al-Zuhrī is that he wrapped himself up out of a fright that befell him when he first saw the angel. The view of Qatāda is that he wrapped himself up in readiness for prayer — this is an interpretation attributed to Qatāda, not his explicit wording. The view of ʿIkrima is that the meaning is: "O you who have been wrapped in (i.e. charged with) prophethood and the message", figuratively — again an interpretation attributed to ʿIkrima; his explicit wording is: "I have entrusted (زمّلت) you with this matter, so carry it out." Abū Jaʿfar said: the clear view is that of al-Zuhrī. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: he was wrapped in a velvet cloth (قطيفة).

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: The mīm [of قُمِ] has kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the wāw was not restored because the vowel is not permanent. On the meaning of قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا there are three views: [first,] that this is not an obligation; what indicates this is that after it comes نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا, and obligations are not like that. The second view is that it is abrogated — the end of the sūra abrogated it; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. The third view is that it was an obligation, and the one addressed by it is the Prophet ﷺ, since He, Mighty and Majestic, did not say "Stand (pl.)". «نصفه» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "stand half of it". أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا: the wāw has ḍamma because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and if you wish you may give it kasra according to the basic rule.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ: [أَوْ expresses] a choice (takhyīr). وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا: its literal sense in the speech of the Arabs is: take your time in reciting it and separate each letter from the letter after it, and do not hurry so that some letters run into others.
It is derived from الرتل. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: in teeth there is الرتل, which is when there are gaps between the teeth, so that they do not overlap one another; one says ثغر رتل ("evenly spaced teeth"). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound, clear view. It has also been said: it is from الرّتل meaning weakness and softness; so the meaning is: make the recitation soft and do not hurry by rushing.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: There are two views on its meaning. ʿUrwa said: when revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on his she-camel, it weighed heavily on her until she lowered her neck to the ground. And it has been said: [it is heavy] because of the obligations it contains and the restraint from desires, as Qatāda said: its weight in the Balance is like its weight on a person in this world.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: إِنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ is from نشأ, meaning "to begin". هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً: so most of the readers read it, and this is accusative as clarification (bayān). And وطاء [in the other reading] is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of واطأ, [whose maṣdars are] مواطأة and وطاء. وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا: [قِيلًا is] also clarification.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: It is reported from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar that he read «سبخا» with a dotted khāʾ, i.e. rest and sleep. And in the ḥadīth: «لا تسبّخي عنه», i.e. do not lighten [his sin].

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: تبتيل is the maṣdar of بتّل, [used here] because the meaning is the same; [the verb is] تبتّل, تبتّلا.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ with rafʿ (nominative); and the Kufans read «رب المشرق والمغرب» with khafḍ (genitive). The nominative is good because it is at the beginning of the verse, in the sense "He is the Lord of the East and the West"; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ. If its khabar were فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا, the accusative would be more appropriate for it.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ, i.e. of what hurts you. وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْراً جَمِيلًا: this is avoidance for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as He said: وَإِذا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آياتِنا فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ [al-Anʿām: 68].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ: conjoined to the nūn and the yāʾ [of ذَرْنِي]; and it may be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ is written with an extra wāw after the alif to distinguish between أولي and إلى. وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا: [قَلِيلًا is] a naʿt (adjective) of an [omitted] maṣdar, or an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: إِنَّ لَدَيْنا أَنْكالًا: [أَنْكالًا is] the noun of «إنّ»; the singular is نكل. وَجَحِيماً وَطَعاماً ذا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذاباً أَلِيماً (13): all of it is conjoined (nasaq), and the meaning is: "with Us is this".

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: هلت التراب, when you move the bottom of the earth so that its top falls down. Abū ʿUbayd said: it is said of anything you let flow freely — sand, earth, food or the like: قد هلته أهيله هيلا, when you let it flow; so it is مهيل. Abū Jaʿfar said: the original form is مهيول; it underwent weakening (iʿlāl), so the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred to the hāʾ, and two vowelless letters met. The grammarians differed after this: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, since it is additional, and the hāʾ was given kasra because of its proximity to the yāʾ, so one said مهيل. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash claimed that this is wrong; their argument is that the wāw came for a meaning, so it is not dropped — rather the yāʾ was dropped. On this basis they would be obliged to say مهول; so they argued that the hāʾ had been given kasra because of its proximity to the yāʾ, and when the yāʾ was dropped, the wāw turned into yāʾ because of its proximity to the kasra. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a matter of morphology (taṣrīf) and of the obscure parts of grammar. They have all agreed that مهيول, مبيوع, مكيول and مغيوم are permissible.
Abū Zayd said: it is a dialect of Tamīm. ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada said: [al-Basīṭ] 505- يوم رذاذ عليه الدّجن مغيوم (A day of drizzle, overcast with dark cloud, clouded over.) This is permissible in roots with yāʾ, but the Basrans do not permit it in roots with wāw; in their view one may not say خاتم مصووغ or كلام مقوول, because of the heaviness of this, since two wāws and a ḍamma have come together, and they find even one heavy and avoid it. [Allah,] Mighty and Majestic, said: وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ [al-Mursalāt: 11] — so it is in the agreed-upon Muṣḥaf. The poet said: [al-Rajaz] 506- لكلّ دهر قد لبست أثؤبا (For every age I have worn [different] garments.) — he replaced the wāw with a hamza. The grammarians permitted رمل مهول and ثوب مبوع, constructing it on بوع الثوب «[Translator's note: the source has «ينوه», apparently «بنوه», "they constructed it".]», replacing the yāʾ with wāw because of the ḍamma before it. Al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 507-
ألم تر أنّ الملك قد شون وجهه ... ونبع بلاد الله قد صار عوسجا
(Have you not seen that the face of kingship has been disfigured, and the nabʿ-wood of Allah's lands has become boxthorn?)
He means «شين». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 508-
ويأوي إلى زغب مساكين دونهم ... فلا لا تخطّاه الرّكاب مهوب
(And he returns to downy, wretched chicks, beyond whom is a fearsome desert that riders do not cross.)
And the highest usage is the one the Qur'an came with. ʿĀʾidh ibn Miḥṣan ibn Thaʿlaba said:
[al-Wāfir] 509-
فأبقى باطلي والحدّ منها ... كدكّان الدّرابنة المطين ]
(So my idle play and my earnest left of her [a she-camel] something like the clay-plastered bench of the doorkeepers.)

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا: the nūn and the second alif [i.e. نا in أَرْسَلْنا] are in the position of rafʿ (nominative), and the first [in إِنَّا] is in the position of naṣb (accusative); the two pronouns are identical [in form] because they are not inflected. شاهِداً عَلَيْكُمْ is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول. كَما أَرْسَلْنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا: the kāf is in the position of naṣb.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ: the first رسول is indefinite because it had not been mentioned before, and the second is definite because it has already been mentioned. For this reason «سلام عليك» is written at the beginning of letters and «والسّلام» at their end; and for this reason some scholars preferred, in the first salutation of the prayer, سلام عليكم, and in the second, السّلام عليكم — and that is the preferred usage in the speech of the Arabs. فَأَخَذْناهُ أَخْذاً وَبِيلًا: [وَبِيلًا is] a naʿt (adjective) of أخذ. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «وبيلا» means "severe". Abū Jaʿfar said: one says كلأ مستوبل, i.e. [pasture] that is not wholesome. Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدانَ شِيباً «[Translator's note: the variant wording of Ibn Masʿūd is not shown in the source; the text quoted is the standard reading.]». Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading is by way of explanation (tafsīr). In يجعل there is a pronoun referring back to اليوم; and the pronoun may refer back to the name of Allah, in which case there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "[on which] He makes the children grey-haired in it".

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ: He did not say منفطرة, although السماء is feminine. There are three views on this. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is as you say معضّل, meaning it by way of attribution (nasab) [i.e. "possessing splitting"]. And it has been said: the masculine is construed according to the meaning of "ceiling" (السقف). The third view is that of al-Farrāʾ: that السماء is treated both as feminine and as masculine, and this came as masculine; and he recited: [al-Wāfir] 510-
فلو رفع السّماء إليه قوما ... لحقنا بالنّجوم مع السحاب
(Had the sky (masc.) raised a people up to it, we would have reached the stars along with the clouds.)
كانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا, i.e. there is no failing in His promise; and He has promised that these things will take place at the Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ, i.e. these things that will take place at the Resurrection are an admonition; and Qatāda said: it means the Qur'an. فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا: he said: i.e. through their obedience.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ «[Translator's note: the source prints the vowels of the accusative here, although the genitive reading is meant.]», conjoined to ثلثي الليل; this is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ. ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read نِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ, conjoined to أدنى. And Ibn Kathīr read وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ «[Translator's note: the source prints the same vowels as the previous reading; what is meant is apparently a reading with the ḍamma dropped, i.e. وَنِصْفْهُ وَثُلْثَهُ.]», dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness. Abū ʿUbayd chose the genitive and argued that after it comes عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ; he said: so how could they stand half of it? Abū Jaʿfar said:
Both readings have been read by the community [of readers]. The construction of the genitive is: "and you stand «[Translator's note: the source has «ويا قوم», apparently a corruption of «وتقوم».]» less than half of it and less than a third of it".
And the construction of the accusative is: "less than two thirds of the night" — and that is more than half — at one time, "and you stand half of it" at another time, "and you stand a third of it" at another time. The argument from عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ has no sense, because He did not report that they said "we stood half of it"; He only reported the reality of what He knows. Al-Farrāʾ reversed his [Abū ʿUbayd's] position and chose the accusative, because in his view the meaning is more fitting with it, since he considers "and less than half of it" unlikely, because in his view it only explains "a little", not "the least of the little". But if it were as he said, it would be نصفه without a wāw, so as to be an explanation of أدنى. The safe course in this, for people of religion, when both readings are soundly transmitted from the community, is not to say that one of them is better than the other, because both of them come from the Prophet ﷺ, so whoever says that incurs sin. The leading Companions, may Allah have mercy on them, used to censure such things. And al-Farrāʾ permitted: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ — the accusative of «ثلثه», conjoined to «أدنى», and the genitive of نِصْفَهُ «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, although it describes the genitive.]», conjoined to ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ; and he argued from the ḥadīth:
"The Prophet's prayer [at night] extended to a third of the night." This too is among the things it is disliked to set against the reading of the community — something that has not been read, and a ḥadīth which, even if it is sound, contains no proof. وَطائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ: some scholars argued from this and took it as evidence that the night prayer is not an obligation; he said: if it were an obligation, they would all have stood. وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ, i.e. He measures their hours and times. عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ: al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "that you would not be able to bear it"; and al-Farrāʾ said: "that you would not keep [count of] it". فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ: He turned back for you to what is easier for you; and التوبة in the language means returning. فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضى: the construction according to Sībawayh is: «[Translator's note: something appears to have dropped out of the source here (presumably that أَنْ is the lightened form of أنّ with an implied pronoun).]» He made it feminine yet made سيكون masculine, because it is a non-real feminine. وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ: conjoined to «مرضى», and likewise وَآخَرُونَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ. For this reason a group of scholars considered standing in the night recommended, even if only the smallest amount, and the ḥadīth on it from the Prophet ﷺ is emphatic. وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً: Ibn Zayd said: [this means] the supererogatory acts besides zakāh. وَما تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْراً وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْراً, i.e. than what you spent. You put «خيرا» in the accusative because it is the khabar (second object) of «تجدوه», and هُوَ is redundant (zāʾida), for separation (faṣl). وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ, i.e. for your sins and your shortcomings. إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ, i.e. [forgiving] of all the punishment of whoever repents; رَحِيمٌ to him, not punishing him after repentance.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative; (المزمّل) badal (substitute) of أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it — following it in the nominative in form; (الليل) adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قم), (إلّا) for exception; (قليلا) excepted, accusative.
The clause «the vocative ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «قم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the vocative.
(نصفه) badal of (قليلا), accusative; (أو) conjunction for giving a choice; (منه) attached to (انقص), (عليه) attached to (زد), (ترتيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «انقص ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the vocative.
The clause «زد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause انقص.
The clause «رتّل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the answer of the vocative.

* Morphology:
(المّزمّل): active participle from the five-letter (تزمّل), meaning "he wrapped himself in his garment" — according to most views [Note: It has been said: the one wrapped in prophethood or in the Qur'an..]; its pattern is متفعّل.. In it there is substitution (ibdāl): its origin is المتزمّل; the tāʾ was changed to zāy, then made quiescent so that assimilation could be completed with the fāʾ of the word, which is the zāy.
(قم): in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion. It is the imperative of the hollow triliteral قام; its origin is قوم, with ḍamma then two sukūns; the weak letter was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents. Its pattern is فل, with ḍamma then sukūn, because its fāʾ has ḍamma in the imperfect. (نصفه): a noun for one of two parts of a thing when they are equal; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn — and the fāʾ may take fatḥa or ḍamma — its plural is أنصاف on the pattern أفعال.
(زد): the iʿlāl in it is as in (قم) and by analogy with it; its pattern is فل, with kasra then sukūn, because the fāʾ has kasra in the imperfect.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا».
I.e. pray the night except a little. Standing is a part of the prayer; so He expressed it by the part, which is standing, and meant the whole, which is prayer. The relation of the trope is part-to-whole (juzʾiyya).

* Benefits:
- The striving of spirit and body:
The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions used to stand in prayer at night, from half to two-thirds of it. A man among them did not know when a third of the night was, or when half of it, or when two-thirds of it; so he would stand the whole night until morning, fearing that he would not observe the obligatory amount. That became so hard on them that their feet swelled. So Allah had mercy on them, lightened it for them, and abrogated it with His saying: «فَاقْرَؤُا ما تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ». It has been said: there is no sūra in the Qur'an whose end abrogated its beginning except this sūra. Between the revelation of its beginning and the revelation of its end there was a year; and it has been said: sixteen months. Standing at night was obligatory, then after that it was abrogated for the community by the five prayers. Its obligation remained established upon the Prophet ﷺ by the saying of Allah the Exalted: (ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا).
From Saʿd ibn Hishām, who said: I went to ʿĀʾisha and said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: Do you not read the Qur'an? I said: Yes. She said: Then the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur'an. I said: And the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? She said: Do you not read al-Muzzammil? I said:
Yes. She said: Allah made standing obligatory at the beginning of this sūra, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and Allah withheld its conclusion in heaven for twelve months; then He sent down the lightening at the end of this sūra, and standing at night became voluntary after being obligatory.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(عليك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سنلقي), (هي) separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: It may be a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is أشدّ, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.], (وطئا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أقوم قيلا) like أشدّ وطئا.
The clause «إنّا سنلقي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سنلقي ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ ناشئة.. أشدّ» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(ناشئة): either the feminine of ناشئ, active participle from the triliteral نشأ, its pattern being فاعل, by which the soul that rises at night for worship is described.. or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning the night vigil, like العاقبة.. It has been said that it is the plural of ناشئ, a non-analogical plural.. And it has been said that it is the first hours of the night, or the acts of obedience that arise in it.
(وطئا): a non-analogical (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb وطأ, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); (في النهار) attached to the omitted khabar [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (سبحا).], (سبحا) noun of إنّ, accusative. The clause «إنّ لك في النهار سبحا ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(سبحا): maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral سبح, meaning "to run" or "to move about in water"; it has been borrowed for going about one's needs. Its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(طويلا): ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral طال; its pattern is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهارِ سَبْحاً طَوِيلًا».
I.e. moving about and occupying yourself with your important affairs, and being busy with your preoccupations, so you cannot devote yourself to worship; so keep to it at night. The original sense of السبح is swift passage through water; it was borrowed for going in general.
They recited the poet's saying: أباحوا لكم شرق البلاد وغربها ... ففيها لكم يا صاح سبح من السبح
(They have opened to you the east of the lands and the west; in them, my friend, you have ample room to roam.)
As for the reading with khāʾ, سبخا, it is a metaphor from سبخ الصوف, which is carding wool and spreading its parts, for the spreading of worry and the dispersal of the heart among preoccupations.

safi-cedvel:8-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إليه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تبتّل), (تبتيلا) an object (mafʿūl) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) is meant], accusative, standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) because it meets it in derivation.
The clause «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تبتّل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
9- (ربّ) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لا إله إلّا هو.], (لا) the lā of generic negation; (إلّا) for exception; (هو) detached pronoun in the position of a nominative, badal (substitute) of the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar of لا, i.e. "there is no god existing except He"; (الفاء) linking to the answer of the condition; (وكيلا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The clause «(هو) ربّ ...» has no grammatical position: causal [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) of ربّك.].
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of a nominative, a second khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ (هو).
The clause «اتّخذه ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want success in your deeds, then take Him as a guardian".
10- (الواو) conjunction; (ما) maṣdar particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted and the clause being its ṣila.], (هجرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (اصبر).
The clause «اصبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اذكر.
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «اهجرهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اصبر.
11- (الواو) conjunction in the three places [Note: Or the second is the wāw of accompaniment, and (المكذّبين) is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).. Ibn Hishām said: there is no wāw of accompaniment in the Noble Qur'an.], (المكذّبين) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first-person pronoun that is the object in (ذرني) [Note: I.e. "I will suffice you against them".] (أولي) naʿt (adjective) of المكذّبين, accusative; (قليلا) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), standing in for the adverb of time, i.e. a short time [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, i.e. a short respite.].
The clause «ذرني ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اصبر.
The clause «مهّلهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اصبر.
12- (لدينا) adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, attached to the khabar of إنّ; (ذا) naʿt of (طعاما), accusative..
The clause «إنّ لدينا أنكالا ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
14- (يوم) adverb attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār) to which لدينا is attached [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt of (عذابا), i.e. "a punishment occurring on the day the earth quakes"..], (مهيلا) naʿt of (كثيبا), accusative.
The clause «ترجف الأرض ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كانت الجبال ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause ترجف, i.e. "they will be"..

* Morphology:
(10) هجرا: maṣdar of the triliteral هجر; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(11) النعمة: a maṣdar meaning enjoyment and comfort; its pattern is فعلة, like the maṣdar of single instance..
(12) أنكالا: plural of نكل, meaning a heavy fetter; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn, and the plural is أفعال.
(13) غصّة: a noun for the state a person is in when he chokes on something; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(14) كثيبا: a noun for heaped-up sand; its pattern is فعيل.
(مهيلا): passive participle from the triliteral (هال), of the class of ضرب, on the pattern of مبيع. In it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion, and there is disagreement between Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī over the place of the deletion, as to whether what was deleted is the wāw or the yāʾ, since its origin is مهيول.

* Rhetoric:
Antithesis (ṭibāq): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ».
For He, Glorified and Exalted, set the east and the west in antithesis in this noble verse.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(إليكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), (عليكم) attached to (شاهدا), (ما) maṣdar particle; (إلى فرعون) attached to the second (أرسلنا).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أرسلنا ...) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is أرسلنا إليكم.
The clause «إنّا أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أرسلنا (the second)» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
16- (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (أخذا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «عصى فرعون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption.
The clause «أخذناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عصى فرعون.

* Morphology:
(وبيلا): ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral وبل, of the class of وعد, i.e. "it became severe"; its pattern is فعيل.. In al-Miṣbāḥ: الوبيل is like الوخيم (unwholesome) in pattern and meaning.

* Benefits:
- A question and a fatwā:
Al-Rashīd wrote one night to the judge Abū Yūsuf, asking him about the saying of the poet:
فإن ترفقي يا هند فالرفق أيمن وإن تخرقي يا هند فالخرق أشأم فأنت طلاق والطلاق عزيمة ... ثلاث، ومن يخرق أعق وأظلم
(If you are gentle, O Hind, gentleness is more blessed; and if you are rough, O Hind, roughness is more ill-omened. So you are divorced, and divorce is a resolve — three; and whoever is rough is the most undutiful and unjust.)
He said: What is binding on him if he makes (ثلاث) nominative, and if he makes it accusative? Abū Yūsuf said: I said: This is a grammatical-juristic question, and I am not safe from error if I give an opinion on it. So I went to al-Kisāʾī, who was in his bed, and asked him. He said: If he makes ثلاثا nominative, she is divorced once, because he said «أنت طلاق» and then informed that complete divorce is three. If he makes it accusative, she is divorced three times, because its meaning is "you are divorced three times", and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause. So I wrote that to al-Rashīd, and he sent me prizes, which I directed to al-Kisāʾī.
And I say: What is correct is that both the nominative and the accusative admit the occurrence of the three and the occurrence of the one. As for the nominative, it is because (أل) in الطلاق is either for the genus figuratively, as you say «زيد الرجل» (Zayd is the man), i.e. he is the man worth reckoning with; or for the previously-mentioned reference (al-ʿahd al-dhikrī), like it in the saying of Allah the Exalted (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شاهِداً عَلَيْكُمْ كَما أَرْسَلْنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا، فَعَصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْناهُ أَخْذاً وَبِيلًا), i.e. "and this mentioned divorce is a resolve of three". It cannot be for the genus in the true sense, lest it entail predicating the particular of the general, as when it is said «الحيوان إنسان» (the animal is a human), which is false, since not every animal is a human, nor is every divorce a resolve or three. So on the referential reading the three occur, and on the generic reading one occurs, as al-Kisāʾī said. As for the accusative: it admits being a mafʿūl muṭlaq, in which case it requires the occurrence of the triple divorce, since the meaning is "so you are divorced three times", with his saying «والطلاق عزيمة» interposed between them; and it admits being a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in عزيمة, in which case the occurrence of the three is not necessary, because the meaning is "and divorce is a resolve when it occurs as three", so only what he intended takes effect. This is what the meaning of the wording requires, regardless of anything else. As for what this particular poet intended, it is the three, because of his saying afterwards:
فبيني بها إن كنت غير رفيقة ... وما لامرئ بعد الثلاث مقدّم
(So be separated by them, if you are not gentle; and after the three there is no going back for any man.)

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking to the answer of an implied condition; (كيف) interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of تتّقون; (كفرتم) past verb in the position of a jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (يوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), whose governor is تتّقون, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the punishment of a day" [Note: Or its governor is كفرتم in the sense of جحدتم (you denied).. It may also be accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "you disbelieved in a day".], accusative; and the agent of (يجعل) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to (يوما) — or to Allah —; (شيبا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «تتّقون ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if you deny the Day of Resurrection, then how will you guard against the punishment of Allah".
The clause «كفرتم ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.. and the answer of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «يجعل ...» is in the position of an accusative, naʿt (adjective) of (يوما) [Note: If the agent in (يجعل) refers to Allah, then in the clause there is an implied linking pronoun, i.e. "He makes the children grey-haired in it".].
18- (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (منفطر) — and (الباء) is causal or locative, and it may be instrumental — and the pronoun in (وعده) refers to Allah.
The clause «السماء منفطر ...» is in the position of an accusative, second naʿt of (يوما).
The clause «كان وعده مفعولا» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: The maṣdar (وعد) is annexed to its agent, who is Allah. The pronoun may refer to the day, in which case the maṣdar is annexed to its object and the agent is omitted; in that case the clause becomes causal.].

* Morphology:
(17) شيبا: plural of أشيب, ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral شاب, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is أفعل. The pattern of شيب is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the shīn was given kasra to suit the yāʾ.. In the feminine one does not say شيباء, but rather شائبة or شمطاء.
(18) منفطر: active participle from the five-letter انفطر; its pattern is منفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. The word came in the masculine because the form is a form of attribution (nasab), i.e. "possessing splitting", like امرأة مرضع (a suckling woman).. The form may be one in which masculine and feminine are the same, or it is because السماء is a generic noun.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدانَ شِيباً».
A metonymy for terror and severity. Of a severe day it is said: a day that turns the forelocks of children grey.
Its basis is that when worries and sorrows mount upon a person, greyness comes quickly to him.

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (من) jussivising conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the object of (شاء) is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "wills salvation" or "faith"; (اتّخذ) past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of the condition; (إلى ربّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «إنّ هذه تذكرة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من شاء ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «شاء ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «اتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(من ثلثي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أدنى), (نصفه) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدنى, accusative, and likewise (ثلثه). [Translator's note: this parsing follows the reading نصفَه وثلثَه with the accusative; in the reading of Ḥafṣ the two words are genitive, conjoined to ثلثي.]
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّك تقوم..) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
(الواو) conjunction; (طائفة) conjoined to the pronoun that is the agent of تقوم [Note: The conjunction came without emphasis by a detached pronoun because of the presence of a separating element.], (من الذين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (طائفة), (معك) adverb, accusative, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; (الواو) conjunction before the Name of Majesty; (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted [Note: Or it is the pronoun of the plural addressee, i.e. "that you will not be able to reckon it".], (الفاء) conjunction; (عليكم) attached to (تاب).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن تحصوه ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of علم.
(الفاء) linking to the answer of an implied condition; (ما) relative noun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من القرآن) tamyīz (specification) of the returning pronoun [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the returning pronoun.] (علم أن) like the first; (منكم) attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of سيكون; (آخرون) conjoined to مرضى; (في الأرض) attached to (يضربون) by making it include the meaning of يسعون or يسافرون; (من فضل) attached to (يبتغون), (في سبيل) attached to (يقاتلون) ..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن سيكون..) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of the second علم.
(الفاء) conjunction; (ما تيسّر منه) like ما تيسّر من القرآن; (قرضا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it meets it in derivation [Note: The second object is omitted. (قرضا) may be the second object if it means the money lent.], (الواو) parenthetical; (ما) jussivising conditional noun in the position of an accusative, a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (لأنفسكم) attached to (تقدّموا) (من خير) tamyīz of ما [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of (ما).], (عند) adverb, accusative, attached to a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (تجدوه) [Note: Or attached to (تجدوه).], (هو) separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: It was permissible for it to separate between a definite and an indefinite — not between two definites — because the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) (خيرا) is treated as definite, since after it comes the thing surpassed, in the genitive with من — both implied — i.e. "better than what you sent forward".] (خيرا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (أجرا) tamyīz, accusative.. (الواو) conjunction..
The clause «إنّ ربّك يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تقوم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «الله يقدّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يقدّر ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «علم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption with the force of a causal clause [Note: Or it is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of يقدّر, with قد implied.].
The clause «لن تحصوه ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
The clause «تاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause علم..
The clause «اقرؤوا ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if you desire reward, then recite".
The clause «تيسّر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «علم ... (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سيكون منكم مرضى ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
The clause «يضربون ...» is in the position of a nominative, naʿt of (آخرون).
The clause «يبتغون ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of يضربون.
The clause «يقاتلون ...» is in the position of a nominative, naʿt of the second (آخرون).
The clause «اقرؤوا ...» is the answer of an implied condition [Note: Like the first clause اقرؤوا.].
The clause «تيسّر (the second)» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «أقيموا ...» is conjoined to the clause اقرؤوا.
The clause «آتوا ...» is conjoined to the clause اقرؤوا.
The clause «تقدّموا ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, for giving a reason.
The clause «تجدوه ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «استغفروا ...» is conjoined to the clause أقيموا الصلاة.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور ...» has no grammatical position: causal.

* Morphology:
(تحصوه): in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by quiescence and by deletion. Its origin is تحصيوه — with a yāʾ bearing ḍamma after the ṣād —; the yāʾ was made quiescent because of heaviness, then deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents. Its pattern is تفعوه..

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ».
I.e. a time less than them. أدنى is used for it — an elative from دنا, "to be near" — because when the distance between two things is near, the intervening spaces between them are few. So in it there is a majāz mursal, because nearness entails few intervening spaces between two things; so it is used for what it entails, or for paucity in general.
It is also permissible to regard it as a likening of nearness to paucity, so that there would be a metaphor (istiʿāra); but the majāz mursal is nearer.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً نِّصْفَهُ}: People have said a great deal about this, and have used it as evidence for the permissibility of excepting the majority and the half, with objections and replies to them. Here I set it out in a refined form, with the help of Allah the Exalted.

Know that this verse has eight possible analyses. The first: that «نصفَه» is a badal (substitute) for «الليلَ», a partial substitute of the whole (badal baʿḍ min kull), and «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the half, as if it were said: "Stand less than half of the night." The pronoun in «مِنْه» and «عليه» refers back to the half.

The meaning is a choice between two matters: between standing less than half the night definitively, and choosing one of two options, namely reducing from the half or adding to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to him, saying that it entails repetition in the wording, since the implied form becomes: "Stand half the night except a little of the half of the night, or reduce from the half of the night." He said: "This is a construction from which the Quran is to be held free." I say: The analysis is problematic, though not for this reason, for the matter here is easy, but for another reason [which I shall mention shortly, Allah willing].

Abū al-Baqāʾ judged this analysis to be the less preferred, for he said: "The second is that it is a badal from «قليلاً», meaning the half." He said: "And it is closer to the apparent sense of the verse, because He said: «أو انقُصْ منه أو زِدْ عليه», and the hāʾ in both refers to the half. If the exception were from the half, the implied form would be: 'Stand half the night except a little, or reduce from it a little', and the little that is excepted is not determined, so reducing from it is not conceivable." I say: The reply to this is that some of them have determined this little: from al-Kalbī and Muqātil, it is the third, so the little was not undetermined. Moreover, there is a contradiction in his statement, for he said, "The little that is excepted is not determined, so reducing from it is [inconceivable]," thus returning the pronoun to the little, whereas in the first instance he returned it to the half.

Someone might say: This analysis can be struck by a strong problem: that it entails repetition of one and the same meaning. For his saying "Stand half the night except a little" has the sense of "reduce from the night", because that little has the sense of reduction; and if you say "Stand half the night except the little of the half" and "Stand half the night, or reduce from the half", you will find the two to have one meaning. There is subtlety in this, so reflect on it. Al-Ḥawfī mentioned no analysis other than this first one, so you now know what is in it.

Among those who held it was Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj), who said: "«نصفَه» is a badal from «الليل», and «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the half. The pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» refers to the half. The meaning: Stand half the night, or reduce from the half a little, down to the third, or add to it a little, up to the third, or add to it a little, up to the two-thirds. So it is as though He said: Stand two-thirds of the night, or its half, or its third."

I say: The implied forms that they bring out are clear and good, except that the construction does not support them, because of the problem I mentioned to you above.

The second: that «نصفَه» is a badal from «قليلاً». Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you wish, you may make «نصفَه» a badal from «قليلاً», and it is then a choice among three: between standing the half in full, standing less than it, and standing more than it. He described the half as 'little' only in relation to the whole." I say: This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ judged closer than making it a badal from «الليل», as stated above.

However, the Shaykh objected to this and said: "If «نصفَه» is a badal from «إلاَّ قليلاً», then the pronoun in «نصفَه» either refers back to the substituted-for word (mubdal minhu) or to the one from which the exception is made, namely «الليلَ». It cannot refer to the substituted-for word, because it would then be an exception of something unknown from something unknown, the implied form being: 'except a little, half of the little', and this has no valid meaning at all. If the pronoun refers to «الليل», there is no benefit in making the exception from «الليل», since it would be shorter, clearer and further from confusion to say: 'Stand the night, half of it.' We have already refuted the view of whoever said that «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the badal, namely «نصفَه», and that the implied form is: 'Stand the night, half of it, except a little of it,' that is, of the half. Moreover, in the claim that «نصفَه» is a badal from «إلاَّ قليلاً» with the pronoun in «نِصفَه» referring to «الليل», there is the application of 'little' to the half, and it also entails that the implied form becomes: 'except its half, so do not stand it, or reduce from the half that you do not stand', and this is a meaning that is not valid and is definitely not what the verse intends."

I say: We hold that the pronoun may refer to either of them, and no objectionable consequence follows. As for what he mentioned, that it would be an exception of something unknown from something unknown, this is rejected; rather it is an exception of something known from something known, for we have shown that the little is a specific quantity, namely the third, and the night is not unknown. Moreover, the exception of an indefinite quantity has occurred. Allah the Exalted said: {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 66]. And He said: {فَشَرِبُواْ مِنْهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 249]. [Translator's note: the next clause is as printed in the source:] He should have said: because it is a badal of something unknown from something unknown. As for what he mentioned, that a shorter and clearer wording is "such and such": the shorter is conceded; that it is confusing is rejected. He departed from the wording he mentioned only because it is more eloquent.

By this analysis, those who said that excepting the half and the majority is permissible have argued. The point of the evidence for the first is that it made «قليلاً» an exception from «الليل», and then explained that little as the half, as if it were said: "Stand the night except its half."

The point of the evidence for the second is that it conjoined «أو زِدْ عليه» to «انقُصْ منه», so it has excepted what exceeds the half, because the pronoun in «مِنْه» and in «عليه» refers to the half. This is weak evidence, because the greater quantity came only through conjunction. It is like your saying: "I owe him ten except five, and a dirham, and a dirham." The excess over the half arises by way of conjunction, not because the exception itself removed the majority.

The third: that «نصفَه» is also a badal from «الليلَ», as in the first analysis, except that the pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» refers to what is less than the half. Al-Zamakhsharī held this, for he said: "If you wish, you may say: since the meaning of {قُمِ الليل إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً نِّصْفَهُ}, when you make the half a badal from «الليل», is 'Stand less than half the night', the pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» returns to the less than half. It is as though it were said: 'Stand less than half the night, or stand less than that lesser amount, or a little more than it,' so the choice, beyond the half, is between it and the third."

The fourth: that «نصفَه» is a badal from «قليلاً» as stated above, except that you make the second «قليلاً» a quarter of the night. Al-Zamakhsharī also clarified this, saying: "When you make «نصفَه» a badal from «قليلاً» and explain it by that, you may make the second «قليلاً» mean half of the half, that is, the quarter, as if it were said: 'or reduce from it a little, its half,' and make the addition to this little, I mean the quarter, half of the quarter, as if it were said: 'or add to it a little, its half.' It is also possible to make the addition, being unrestricted, the completion of the third, so the choice is between the half, the third and the quarter." End of quotation. These analyses that I have related from Abū al-Qāsim (al-Zamakhsharī) bear witness to the breadth of his knowledge of the Book of Allah. When his expression proved too broad for the Shaykh, he said: "How wide is this man's imagination! He allows what is near and what is far." I say: What would it have cost the Shaykh to say: "How wide is this man's knowledge!"

The fifth: that «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the standing, so that you take «الليل» as a generic noun and then say «إلاَّ قليلاً», that is, except the nights whose standing you leave because of a clear excuse and the like. This view is good if one holds that the command is recommended (nadb). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, as a possibility of his own. In his wording it was "those in which you fall short of standing," and I replaced it with "those in which you leave standing." In sum, this goes against the apparent sense and is a remote interpretation.

The sixth: al-Akhfash said: "The original is: 'Stand the night except a little, or its half.'" He said: "Like your saying: 'Give him a dirham, two dirhams, three,'" that is, "or two dirhams or three." This is very weak, because it involves omitting the conjunction, which is not allowed; only something anomalous has occurred, which can be interpreted, such as their saying: "I ate meat, fish, dates." And the other's saying:

4364 - كيف أَصْبَحْتَ كيف أَمْسَيْتَ مِمَّا ... يَزْرَعُ الوُدَّ في فؤادِ الكريم
(Gloss: "How did you wake, how did you spend the evening" is among the things that plant affection in the noble heart.)

meaning: meat and fish and dates, and likewise "how did you wake and how did you spend the evening". People have analysed this as badal al-badāʾ.

The seventh: al-Tabrīzī said: "The command to stand, with the choice of adding and reducing, applies to the two-thirds from the end of the night, because the first third is the time of the ʿatama (the early part of the night after dusk). The exception comes upon what is commanded, so it is as though He said: 'Stand two-thirds of the night except a little,' that is, less than its half, 'or add to it,' that is, to the two-thirds. So the choice of adding and reducing applies to the two-thirds." This is a strange statement that does not emerge from this construction.

The eighth: that «نصفَه» is accusative by the implication of a verb, that is, "stand its half". Makkī related it from others, for he said: "«نصفَه» is a badal from «الليل»; it is also said that it is accusative by the implication of 'stand its half'." I say: In reality this is the very badal analysis he mentioned first, because a badal is on the intention of repeating the governing word.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي}: This clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This verse is a parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ)." Then he said: "By this parenthesis he meant that the night standing he was charged with is among the heavy and difficult obligations with which the Quran came, because the night is the time of rest, repose and stillness, so whoever keeps it alive must oppose his own nature and strive against his soul." End of quotation. He means "parenthetical" in terms of meaning, not in terms of the technical craft (of grammar); that is because His saying {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل هِيَ أَشَدُّ} corresponds to His saying {قُمِ الليل}, so it resembles a parenthesis in that it enters between these two corresponding statements.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل}: There are several analyses of «الناشئة». The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted noun, that is, "the soul that arises in the night," which rises from its bed for worship, that is, gets up and rises. It is from "the cloud arose (nashaʾat)" when it rose, and "he arose (nashaʾa) from his place" and "nashaza" when he got up. He said:

4365 - نَشَأْنا إلى خُوْصٍ بَرَى نَيَّها السُّرى ... وأَشْرَف منها مُشْرِفاتِ القَماحِدِ
(Gloss: We rose toward sunken-eyed camels whose fat the night-travel had worn away, while their high-standing parts towered above.)

The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning standing at night, being a maṣdar of «نَشَأَ» when he stood and rose, so it is like «العافية». Both were said by al-Zamakhsharī.

The third: that it is in the language of the Abyssinians; "the man nashaʾa" means he stood at night. The Shaykh said: "On this, it is the plural of «ناشِىء», that is, one who stands" [Translator's note: the source text repeats "that is, one who stands" here, an apparent printing duplication]. I say: He means that it is an adjective for something that conveys plurality, that is, a group or a company that arises; otherwise, a fāʿil form is not pluralised as fāʿila.

The fourth: that «ناشئة الليل» are its hours, because they arise one after another. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan restricted them to what comes after the ʿishāʾ, and what is before it is not nāshiʾa. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, specified it in another sense: that it be after sleep, so if no sleep preceded it, it would not be nāshiʾa.

His saying: {وَطْأً}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with kasra on the wāw and fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, followed by an alif (wiṭāʾan). The rest read it with fatḥa on the wāw and sukūn on the ṭāʾ. Qatāda and Shibl, on the authority of the people of Mecca, read «وِطْئاً». The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words suggests that it was read with fatḥa on the wāw with lengthening, for he said: "«وِطاء» with kasra on the wāw means muwāṭaʾa (agreement); with fatḥa it is a noun for the maṣdar; and «وَطْئاً» is on the pattern faʿl, and is the maṣdar of «وَطِىءَ»." So «الوِطاء» is the maṣdar of «واطَأَ», like «قِتال», the maṣdar of «قاتَل». The meaning: it is stronger in agreement, that is, the heart of the soul agrees with its tongue, if you mean the soul; or the heart of the one standing agrees therein with his tongue, if you mean the standing or the worship or the hours; or it is stronger in conformity with what is intended of humility and sincerity. And «الوَطْء» with fatḥa or kasra in the sense: firmer in footing and further from slipping; or heavier and harsher on the one praying than the prayer of the day, from his saying, peace be upon him: "O Allah, press down Your tread upon Muḍar." And on every analysis, its accusative status is as tamyīz (specification).

His saying: {وَأَقْوَمُ}: Al-Zamakhsharī related: "That Anas read «وأَصْوَبُ قِيلاً», and it was said to him: 'O Abū Ḥamza, it is only «وأقومُ»!' He said: 'Aqwam, aṣwab and ahyaʾ are the same.' And that Abū Sirār al-Ghanawī read «فحاسُوا خلالَ الديارِ» with the unpointed ḥāʾ, and it was said to him: 'It is with jīm.' He said: 'Ḥāsū and jāsū are the same.'" I say: He has a purpose in these two reports, namely the permissibility of reciting the Quran by meaning, but there is no evidence in this, because it is an explanation of meaning. Moreover, what we have before us is a mutawātir Quran, and this report is a single-chain report (āḥād). It has already been mentioned that Abū al-Dardāʾ used to teach men to recite {إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزقوم طَعَامُ الأثيم} [al-Dukhān: 44], and the man kept saying: "al-yatīm." When he grew weary of him he said: "The food of the wicked (al-fājir), you there." Those who hold that it is permissible used this as evidence for it. There is no evidence in it, because Abū al-Dardāʾ's aim [was] to explain the meaning, so he brought a clarifying expression.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {سَبْحَاً}: The majority read it with the unpointed ḥāʾ, and it is the maṣdar of «سَبَحَ». It is a metaphor: swimming in water, which is going far in it, is borrowed for the busy handling of one's needs. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, ʿIkrima and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «سَبْخاً» with the pointed khāʾ. They differed in its explanation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a metaphor from «سَبْخ الصُّوف», which is to fluff it and spread out its parts, for the spreading of worry and the scattering of the heart by distractions. It is also said: «التَّسبيخ» means lightening. Al-Aṣmaʿī related: «سَبَخَ الله عَنَك الحُمَّى», that is, He lightened it for you. The poet said:

4366 - فَسَبِّخْ عليكَ الهَمَّ واعلمْ بأنَّه ... إذا قَدَّرَ الرحمنُ شيئاً فكائِنُ
(Gloss: Lighten your worry, and know that when the Merciful decrees something, it will come to be.)

that is, lighten. From it comes «لا تُسَبِّخي بدُعائِك», that is, do not lighten. It is also said: «التَّسْبيخ» is stretching. One says «سَبِّخي قُطْنَكِ», that is, stretch it out, and «السَّبيخة» is a piece of cotton; the plural is «سبائخ». Al-Akhṭal said, describing a hunter and dogs:

4367 - فأَرْسَلوهُنَّ يُذْرِيْنَ الترابَ كما ... يُذْرِيْ سبائخَ قُطْنٍ نَدْفُ أوتارِ
(Gloss: They sent them off, scattering the dust as the carding of bowstrings scatters tufts of cotton.)

Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said: "Ibn Yaʿmar and ʿIkrima read «سَبْخاً» with the pointed khāʾ and said: its meaning is sleep, that is, he sleeps by day so as to seek help from it for standing at night. This reading may bear a meaning other than this, but the two explained it, so there is no going beyond it." I say: This needs consideration, because the most that can be said is that the two transmitted this reading and its explanation appeared to them to be as they stated, and it does not follow from that that an explanation of the word other than what they mentioned is impermissible.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {تَبْتِيلاً}: It is a maṣdar not on the pattern of its verb (maṣdar ʿalā ghayr al-maṣdar), standing in the place of «التَّبَتُّل», because the maṣdar of «تَفَعَّل» is like «تَصَرَّفَ تَصَرُّفاً» and «تكرَّمَ تكرُّماً», whereas «التفعيل» is the maṣdar of «فَعَّل», like «صَرَّف تَصْرِيفاً». Similar is the poet's saying:

4367 - وقد تَطَوَّيْتُ انْطِواءَ الحِضْبِ
(Gloss: I have coiled myself up as the male snake coils.) [Translator's note: the verse number 4367 repeats the number given to the previous verse in the preceding entry, as printed in the source; only a single hemistich is quoted.]

So he put the form of inflection (infiʿāl) in the place of the form «التَّفَعُّل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the meaning of «تَبَتَّل» is «بَتَّلَ نفسَه», so it was brought on its meaning, out of regard for the rhyme-endings of the verses (fawāṣil)." «التبتُّل» is severance. From it comes «امرأة بتولٌ», that is, a woman cut off from marriage, and «بَتَلْتُ الحَبْلَ» means I cut the rope. Al-Layth said: «البَتْلُ» is the separation of one thing from another. They said: «طَلْقَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ» and «هِبَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ», meaning its being cut off from its owner. So «التبتيل» is abandoning marriage and being abstinent about it. What is meant by it in the noble verse is devotion to the worship of Allah the Exalted without abandoning marriage. In the hadith: "that he forbade tabattul," that is, severance from marriage; from it the monk is called «مُتَبتِّلاً» because of his severance from marriage. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

4368 - تُضِيْءُ الظلامَ بالعَشِيِّ كأنَّها ... منارةُ مُمْسَى راهِبٍ مُتَبَتِّلِ
(Gloss: She lights up the darkness in the evening as though she were the lamp-tower of a celibate monk's evening quarters.)

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {رَّبُّ المشرق}: The two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza), Abū Bakr (Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim) and Ibn ʿĀmir read «ربِّ المشرق» in the genitive, as an adjective of «ربِّك», or a badal from it, or a clarification of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And from Ibn ʿAbbās, it is as an oath, with the particle of oath omitted, like your saying «اللَّهِ لأفعلَنَّ», and its answer is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, as you say «واللَّهِ لا أحدَ في الدار إلاَّ زيدٌ»." The Shaykh said: "Perhaps this analysis is not sound from Ibn ʿAbbās, because it involves omission of the preposition, which the Basrans permit only with the glorified name Allah specifically; and because a negated nominal clause in the answer to an oath is negated only by «ما» alone, and «لا» negates only a clause beginning with an imperfect verb, commonly, or with a past verb in its sense, rarely, as in his saying:

4369 - رِدُوا فواللَّهِ لا ذُذْناكُمُ أبداً ... ما دام في مائنا وِرْدٌ لوُرَّادِ
(Gloss: Come to the water, for by Allah we will never drive you off, as long as there is any watering left for the waterers in our water.)

Al-Zamakhsharī brought that by way of allowing it and conceding it, and what the grammarians mention is its negation with «ما», as in his saying:

4370 - لَعَمْرُك ما سَعْدٌ بخُلَّةِ آثمٍ ... ولا نَأْنَأٍ يومَ الحِفاظِ ولا حَصِرْ
(Gloss: By your life, Saʿd is no friend of a sinner, nor a weakling on the day of defence of honour, nor one who is constrained.)

I say: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik stated without restriction that a negated clause, whether nominal or verbal, is answered with «ما», «لا», or «إنْ» in the sense of «ما», and this is the apparent position.

The rest of the Seven read it in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the Lord of". This is better, for the connection of the speech with one another. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «رَبَّ» in the accusative, as praise (madḥ). The majority read «المَشْرِقِ والمغربِ» in the singular, whereas ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) and Ibn ʿAbbās read «المشارِقِ والمغارِبِ». In Zayd's reading it is also possible to make «ربَّ» accusative in two other ways. One of them: that it is a badal from «اسمَ ربِّك», or a clarification of it, or an adjective of it, as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, and this follows from the view that the name is the thing named. The second: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation) with an implied verb, that is, "so take the Lord of the East and the West, so take Him," and what is between them is parenthetical.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {والمكذبين}: It may be accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), which is the apparent sense, and it may be accusative by conjunction (nasaq), which is more consistent with the craft of grammar.

His saying: {أُوْلِي النعمة}: It is an adjective (naʿt) of «المكَذِّبين». «النَّعْمَةُ» with fatḥa means living in comfort; with kasra, bestowing favour; with ḍamma, delight. One says «نُعْمُ» and «نُعْمَةُ عَيْنٍ».

His saying: {قَلِيلاً}: It is an adjective of a maṣdar, that is, "a respite (tamhīlan)", or of an omitted adverb of time, that is, "a short time".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {أَنكَالاً}: It is the plural of «نِكْل». There are two views on it; the better known is that it is the shackle (qayd). It is also said to be the iron collar (ghull), but the first is better known. Al-Khansāʾ said:

4371 - دَعاكَ فَقَطَّعْتُ أنكالَهُ ... وقد كُنَّ مِنْ قبلُ لا تُقْطَعُ
(Gloss: He called you, so I cut his shackles, though before that they could not be cut.)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ذَا غُصَّةٍ}: «الغُصَّةُ» is the shajā, that is, what lodges in the throat and cannot be swallowed. One says «غَصَصْتَ» (with kasra), so you are «غاصٌّ» and «غَصَّانُ». He said:

4372 - لو بغيرِ الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... كنتُ كالغَصَّانِ بالماءِ اعتصاري
(Gloss: Had my throat choked on something other than water, I would be like the one who chokes on water, seeking relief in it.)

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ}: There are several analyses of it. The first: that it is accusative by «ذَرْني», which is remote. The second: that it is accusative by the "settling" (istiqrār) to which «لَدَيْنا» is attached. The third: that it is an adjective of «عذاباً», attached to an omitted word, that is, "a punishment occurring on the day when the earth quakes". The fourth: that it is accusative by «أليم». The majority read «تَرْجُفُ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm, active voice; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads it in the passive, from «أَرْجَفَها».

His saying: {مَّهِيلاً}: Its original is «مَهْيُول» like «مَضْروب». The ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was moved to the preceding quiescent letter, the hāʾ, and two quiescent letters met. The grammarians differed about what to do in that case. Sībawayh and his followers dropped the wāw, and it was the more fitting to drop because it is the additional letter, even though the rule is that what is dropped when two quiescent letters meet is the first; they then put kasra on the hāʾ so that the yāʾ is sound, and its pattern is then «مَفِعْل». Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash dropped the yāʾ, because the rule when two quiescent letters meet and one of them must be dropped is that the first is dropped; by their view it should have been said «مَهُوْل», except that they put kasra on the hāʾ for the sake of the yāʾ that had been there, and the wāw was turned into yāʾ; its pattern is then «مَفُوْلاً» in the original form and «مَفِيلاً» after the change.

Makkī said: "All of them allowed it to come in its original form in speech, so you say «مَهْيُوْل» and «مَبْيُوع» and the like, among the roots with yāʾ. If it is of the roots with wāw, it is not allowed to come in its original form according to the Basrans, while the Kufans allowed it, as in «مَقْوُوْل» and «مَصْوُوْغ».
