All of them allowed «مَهُوْل» and «مَبُوْع» according to the dialect of those who say «بُوع المتاعُ» and «قُوِل القولُ», and the difference over what is dropped from it is as stated above." I say: Completing the form in «مَبْيُوع» and «مَهْيُوْل» and their like is the dialect of Tamīm, and dropping is the dialect of the rest of the Arabs. One says: «هِلْتُ الترابَ أَهيلُه هَيْلاً» so it is «مَهِيل». There is also a dialect: «أَهْلتُه» as a quadriliteral verb, «إهالةً», so it is «مُهال», like «أبَعْتُه إباعَةً» so it is «مُباعٌ».

«والكثيبُ» is what is gathered of sand. The plural of paucity is «أَكْثِبَة», and of multitude «كُثْبان» and «كُثُب», like «رَغِيف», «أرْغِفَة», «رُغْفان», «رُغُفُ». Dhū al-Rumma said:

4373 - فقلت لها: لا إنَّ أهليَ جيرةٌ ... لأكثبةِ الدَّهْنا جميعاً وماليا
(Gloss: I said to her: No, my family are neighbours of the dunes of al-Dahnāʾ, all of them, and so is my property.)

«والمَهيلُ» is what pours down under the foot, that is, spills, from «هِلْتُ الترابَ», that is, I threw it down. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «كَثَبْتُ الشيءَ» when you gather it, and from it «الكُثْبةُ» of milk. The ewe said: I am shorn in fleeces and milked in quick small portions."

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول}: He made it definite only because it was mentioned earlier. This is the lām of previous reference (al-ʿahdiyya). When the Arabs mention a noun first and then report about it a second time, they bring it definite with «أل», or bring its pronoun, so that it is not confused with another, for example "I saw a man, and I honoured the man," or "and I honoured him." If you said "and I honoured a man," it would be thought that he was not the first. The verification of this will come at His saying {إِنَّ مَعَ العسر يُسْراً} [al-Sharḥ: 6] and his saying, peace be upon him: "One hardship will never overcome two eases."

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {يَوْماً}: It is accusative either by «تَتَّقُون» as a direct object, loosely speaking. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يوماً» is a direct object, that is: how will you protect yourselves on the Day of Resurrection, and its terror, if you remain in disbelief?" The Shaykh disputed it and said: "«تَتَّقون» is the imperfect of «اتَّقى», and «اتَّقى» does not have the meaning of «وَقَى» so as to be explained by it; «اتَّقى» takes one object, and «وَقَى» takes two. Allah the Exalted said: {وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الجحيم} [al-Dukhān: 56]. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī implied it as «تَقُون أنفسَكم», but «تَتَّقون» does not have the meaning of «يَقُوْن», so it is not made transitive in its manner." End of quotation.

It is also possible that it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), that is: how will you manage piety on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieved in the world? Al-Zamakhsharī said it. It is also possible that it is accusative as a direct object of «كَفَرْتُمْ» if «كَفَرْتُمْ» is taken in the sense of «جَحَدْتُم» (you denied), that is: how will you fear Allah and be in awe of Him if you deny the Day of Resurrection? It cannot be accusative as an adverbial, because they will not disbelieve on that day; rather they will certainly believe. It is also possible that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "if you disbelieved in the Day of Resurrection". The majority read «يوماً» with tanwīn and make the clause after it its adjective. The returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "it makes the children grey-haired on it". Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, and did not address the agent of «يَجْعل»; on this it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, that is, "a day on which Allah makes..." Better than this is to make the returning pronoun latent in «يَجْعَلُ», being its agent, and the attribution of making to the day is by way of exaggeration, that is, the day itself makes the children grey-haired.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يومَ يَجْعَلُ», with the adverbial annexed to the clause. The agent on this is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted. The "making" here means "turning into", so «شِيْباً» is the second object, and it is the plural of «أَشْيَب». The original of the shīn is with ḍamma, but it was given kasra so that the yāʾ is sound, like «أحمر» and «حُمْر». The poet said:

4374 - مِنَّا الذي هُوَ ما إنْ طُرَّ شارِبُه ... والعانِسُون ومنا المُرْدُ والشِّيْبُ
(Gloss: Among us is he whose moustache has not yet sprouted, and the unmarried grown men; among us are the beardless youths and the grey-haired.)

And another said:

4375 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيْباً وشَيَّبْنَنا مُرْدا
(Gloss: [first hemistich missing in the source] They played with us when we were grey-haired, and they turned us grey when we were beardless.)

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ}: It is another adjective, that is, "split open because of its terror." The adjective was not made feminine for one of several reasons. Among them: that «السماء» is interpreted in the sense of «السَّقْف» (the roof). Among them: that it is on the basis of relation (nasab), that is, "possessing splitting," like «مُرْضِعٍ» and «حائضٍ». Among them: that it may be masculine or feminine; al-Farrāʾ recited:

4376 - ولو رَفَعَ السَّماء إليه قوماً ... لَحِقْنا بالسَّماءِ وبالسَّحابِ
(Gloss: Had the sky raised any people up to it, we would have reached the sky and the clouds.)

Among them: that it is a generic noun (ism jins) distinguished from its singular by the tāʾ, so one says «سَماءة»; it has already been mentioned that a generic noun can be both masculine and feminine. For this reason al-Fārisī said: "It is like His saying {جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ} [al-Qamar: 7], {الشجر الأخضر} [Yā Sīn: 80] and {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20]," meaning that it came in one of the two permissible forms. The bāʾ in it is causal (sababiyya), as stated above. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be the bāʾ of instrumentality (istiʿāna), for he said: "The bāʾ in «به» is like it in your saying «فَطَرْتُ العُوْدَ بالقَدُومِ فانْفَطر به»" (I split the wood with the adze, and it split by it).

His saying: {وَعْدُهُ}: The pronoun may refer to Allah the Exalted, even though no mention of Him has preceded, because it is known, so the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. It may also refer to the day, so it is annexed to its object. The agent, which is Allah the Exalted, is then implied.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {مِن ثُلُثَيِ الليل}: The majority read with ḍamma on the lām, which is the original, like «الرُّبُع» and «السُّدُس»; Hishām read it with sukūn for lightness.

His saying: {وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ}: The Kufans and Ibn Kathīr read both in the accusative, and the rest read both in the genitive. In the genitive there is a difficulty, as will come. The accusative is a conjunction (nasaq) upon «أَدْنى», because it has the sense "a time nearer (adnā)", that is, closer; nearness was borrowed for closeness of distance in time. This corresponds to the division at the beginning of the sūra: if he stands less than two-thirds of the night, it is true of him that he stood the night except a little, because the time in which he did not stand would be the third and something of the two-thirds, so His saying «إلاَّ قليلاً» is true of him. As for His saying «ونِصْفَه», it corresponds to His first saying «نِصْفَه». As for His saying «وثُلُثَه», His saying {أَوِ انقص مِنْهُ} may bring the reduction, in the case of the little, to the point where the time is two-thirds of the night. As for His saying {أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ}, when he adds a little to the half, the time is less than the two-thirds. So it corresponds to "less than two-thirds of the night", and His saying {نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقص مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً} is an explanation of the indefinite thing indicated by His saying {قُمِ الليل إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}. On the accusative reading, al-Ḥasan explained «تُحْصُوه» as "you are able for it".

As for the genitive reading, its meaning is that the standing varies: at one time less than two-thirds, at another less than half, at another less than a third; that is because it is impossible for people to know the measure of time given the excuse of sleep. Al-Zamakhsharī clarified all this, saying: "«نصفَه وثلثَه» was read in the accusative, meaning that you stand less than two-thirds, and stand the half and the third; this corresponds to the choice mentioned at the beginning of the sūra: between standing the half in full, standing less than it, which is the third, and standing more than it, which is the less than two-thirds. It was read in the genitive, that is, you stand less than two-thirds and less than the half and the third, and it corresponds to the choice between the half, which is less than the two-thirds, and the third, which is less than the half, and the quarter, which is less than the two-thirds and the third, which is less than the half, and the quarter, which is less than the third, and this is the last analysis." [Translator's note: the source text repeats this list in garbled form, as printed.] End of quotation. By "the last analysis" he means the interpretations he put forward at the beginning of the sūra.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī said: "In the accusative reading there is a difficulty, unless one implies: its half at one time, its third at another, and less than the half and the third at another, so the meaning is sound."

His saying: {وَطَآئِفَةٌ}: It is nominative by conjunction upon the pronoun in «يقومُ»; the separation by the adverbial and what is conjoined to it permitted that.

His saying: {والله يُقَدِّرُ الليل}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Putting His name, the Mighty and Majestic, first as a mubtadaʾ upon which «يُقَدِّرُ» is built is what indicates the sense of exclusivity in determining."

The Shaykh disputed this and said: "If it were said «زيدٌ يحفظُ القرآن», that would not indicate his exclusivity." He took the exclusivity in the verse to be understood from the context, not from what he mentioned.

His saying: {أَنْ لَنْ} and «أَنْ سيكونُ»: both are lightened forms of the heavy «أنّ», and the separator is the negation and the particle of extension (sīn).

His saying: {وَآخَرُونَ}: It is conjoined to «مَرْضَى», that is, He knew that there would be found among you a group who are sick and another group who are travelling. So «يَضْرِبون» is an adjective of «آخرون», and likewise «يَبْتَغون». It is also possible that «يَبْتَغون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَضْرِبون», and «آخرون» is conjoined to «آخرون», and «يقاتِلون» is its adjective.

His saying: {هُوَ خَيْراً}: The majority read «الخير» in the accusative, as a second object. «هو» is either emphasis of the first object or a separator (faṣl). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a badal, which is a mistake, because it would have to agree with what precedes it in case-ending, so one would say «إياه». Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «خيرٌ», so that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «خيرٌ» its khabar. The clause is the second object of «تَجِدوه». Abū Zayd said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm; they put in the nominative what comes after the separator." Sībawayh recited:

4377 - تَحِنُّ إلى ليلى وأنتَ تركتَها ... وكنتَ عليها بالمَلا أنتَ أَقْدَرُ
(Gloss: You long for Layla when it was you who left her, and when you were in the open country you were the more able over her.)

The rhymes are nominative. It is also transmitted as «أقْدَارا» in the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«هو» is a separator, and it is allowed even though it does not fall between two definites, because «أَفْعَلَ مِنْ», in its refusal of the definite article, resembles a definite." I say: This is the well-known view. Some of them allow it with indefinites other than «أفعل».

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {المزمل}: Its origin is «المتزَمِّلُ», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy. One says «تَزَمَّل يتزَمَّلُ تَزَمُّلاً» ("he wrapped himself up"). When assimilation is intended, the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) is brought in, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read according to this original. ʿIkrima read «المُزَمِّل» with a light zāy and a doubled mīm, as an active participle. On this there are two views. One: that its origin is «المُزْتَمِلُ», on the pattern مُفْتَعِل, then the tāʾ was changed to mīm and assimilated; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ, and it is weak. The other: that it is an active participle of «زَمَّل» with doubling, and on this the object is omitted, that is, "the one who wraps his body." It was also read so, except with fatḥa on the mīm, as a passive participle of it, that is, "the one wrapped up." التَّزَمُّل means wrapping oneself. One says «تَزَمَّلَ زيدٌ بكساءٍ», that is, he wrapped himself in a cloak. Dhū al-Rumma said:
4362 - وكائِنْ تَخَطَّتْ ناقتي مِنْ مَفازةٍ ... ومِنْ نائمٍ عن ليلِها مُتَزَمِّلِ
(How many a desert has my she-camel crossed, and how many a sleeper, wrapped up, heedless of his night.) And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4363 - كأنَّ ثبيراً في أفانينِ وَدْقِه ... كبيرُ أُناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّلِ
(As though Thabīr, amid the varieties of its rain, were the chief of a people wrapped in a striped cloak.) This is like the reading of some mentioned above. In the exegesis it is said that he was addressed so because of his wrapping himself in a cloak.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {قُمِ الليل}: The majority read the mīm with kasra, because of the meeting of two silent letters. Abū al-Sammāl read it with ḍamma, following the vowel of the qāf. It was also read with fatḥa, seeking lightness. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "The aim is to escape the meeting of two silent letters, so with whichever vowel the first is moved, the aim is achieved." I say: except that the original is kasra, for a reason the grammarians mentioned. «الليلَ» is an adverbial (ẓarf) for the standing, even if the event occurring in it spans all of it. This is the statement of the Basrans; as for the Kufans, they make this kind a direct object.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (الْمُزَّمِّلُ): its root form is «الْمُتَزَمِّل»; the tāʾ was changed into a zāy and assimilated.
It has also been read with a doubled mīm and an undoubled zāy (الْمُزَمِّل), and there are two views on it. First: it is a doubled-stem form (muḍāʿaf, i.e. Form II), and the object is omitted, i.e. «الْمُزَمِّلُ نَفْسَهُ» (the one who wraps himself). Second: it is on the pattern «مُفْتَعِل», and the fāʾ was changed into a mīm.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (نِصْفَهُ): there are two views on it.
First: it is a badal (substitute) for «اللَّيْل», a substitute of the part for the whole; and «إِلَّا قَلِيلًا» is an exception from «نِصْفَهُ».
Second: it is a badal for «قَلِيلًا», and this is closer to the apparent sense of the verse, because the Exalted said «أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ» and «أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ», and the hāʾ in both refers to the half. If the exception were from the half, the implied form would become: stand half the night [except] a little, or reduce from it a little, i.e. from the remainder; but the little that is excepted is not determined, so reducing from it is unintelligible.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا): [it is read] with a kasra on the wāw, meaning «مُوَاطَأَة» (concordance), and with a fatḥa on it, and this is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar). And «وَطْأً» is on the pattern «فَعْل»; it is the maṣdar of «وَطِئَ» (to tread). It is a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (تَبْتِيلًا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) not on the pattern of [its verb's] maṣdar, occurring in the place of «تَبَتُّل».
It is also said that the meaning is: «بَتِّلْ نَفْسَكَ تَبْتِيلًا» (devote yourself with full devotion).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا (٩)).
The words of the Exalted (رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ): it is read in the genitive as a badal (substitute); in the accusative by the implied verb «أَعْنِي» (I mean), or as a badal for «اسْمَ», or by a verb explained by «فَاتَّخِذْهُ», i.e. «اتَّخِذْ رَبَّ الْمَشْرِقِ» (take the Lord of the East); and in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ with «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ» as the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ): it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). It is also said that it is maʿṭūf (conjoined).
(النَّعْمَةِ) with a fatḥa on the nūn means luxury, and with a kasra means abundance of good.
The words of the Exalted (وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا): i.e. a little respite, or a little time.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا (١٤)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for the [notion of] being established contained in the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ».
It is also said that it is a description of «عَذَابًا», i.e. occurring on the day when it quakes. It is also said that it is an adverb for «أَلِيمًا».
The root form of «مَهِيل» is «مَهْيُول»; according to Sībawayh the wāw was dropped and the yāʾ was made vowelless (sākin); and according to al-Akhfash the yāʾ [was dropped] and the wāw was changed into a yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ. . . (١٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ): He repeated it only with the definite article so that it would be known that it is the first [messenger mentioned]. It is as if He said: «فَعَصَاهُ فِرْعَوْنُ» (so Pharaoh disobeyed him).

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا (١٧) السَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمًا): it is the object of «تَتَّقُونَ», i.e. you guard against the punishment of a day.
It is also said that it is the object of «كَفَرْتُمْ», i.e. [disbelieve] in a day. (يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «اليوم», and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «فِيهِ» (in it).
(مُنْفَطِرٌ) is without the tāʾ [of the feminine] by way of attribution (nasab), i.e. «ذَاتُ انْفِطَارٍ» (possessed of splitting). It is also said that it is masculine by being construed according to the sense of «السَّقْف» (the roof). It is also said: «السماء» is treated as both masculine and feminine.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ وَطَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَنْ لَنْ تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَآخَرُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٢٠)).
The words of the Exalted (وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ): in the genitive, construed with «ثُلُثَيِ», and in the accusative, construed with «أَدْنَى». (وَطَائِفَةٌ) is conjoined to the agent pronoun [in «تَقُومُ»], and the separation [by intervening words] took the place of the emphasis (tawkīd).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ سَيَكُونُ): «أَنْ» is lightened from the heavy «أَنَّ», the sīn is a compensation for its lightening, and its noun is omitted. (يَبْتَغُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَضْرِبُونَ».
The words of the Exalted (هُوَ خَيْرًا): «هُوَ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a badal (substitute), or a tawkīd (emphasis), and «خَيْرًا» is the second object.

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Muzzammil
Meccan, except for two verses at its end, which are Medinan
﷽
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها المُزَّمِّلُ﴾ ﴿قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ ("O you wrapped in garments, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little"): this is an address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). It was said that this was revealed to him while a velvet wrap was over him. «المُزَّمِّل» is originally «المُتَزَمِّل», but the tāʾ is assimilated into the zāy because of its closeness to it. One says «تَزَمَّلَ فُلانٌ» when someone wraps himself in his clothes, and everything wrapped has been «زُمِّلَ». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎كَأنَّ أبانًا في أفانِينِ ودْقِهِ ∗∗∗ كَبِيرُ أُناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّلِ
(As though [Mount] Abān, amid the varied sheets of its downpour, were a chief of men wrapped in a striped cloak.)
And it was said that he was wrapped up in the attire of prayer.
His saying: ﴿قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ ﴿نِصْفَهُ أوِ انْقُصْ مِنهُ قَلِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] ﴿أوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4] ("Stand the night, except a little — half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it"): the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that «نِصْفَهُ» is a badal (substitute) for «اللَّيْلَ», as you say «ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا رَأْسَهُ» ("I struck Zayd, his head"): you mentioned «زَيْدًا» only to emphasise the statement, and it is more emphatic than your saying «ضَرَبْتُ رَأْسَ زَيْدٍ» ("I struck Zayd's head"). So the meaning is: "Stand half the night except a little, or subtract from the half, or add to the half." He mentioned ﴿أوِ انْقُصْ مِنهُ قَلِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] in the meaning of «إلّا قَلِيلًا», but it was mentioned together with the addition; so the meaning is: "Stand half the night, or subtract from half the night, or add to a half." This — and Allah knows best — was before the obligation of the five prayers came.
The meaning of ﴿وَرَتِّلِ القُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4] ("and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation") is: make it clear distinctly. Clarity is not achieved by hurrying through the Qur'an; it is achieved only by making all the letters clear and giving them their full due in fullness of pronunciation.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿واصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ واهْجُرْهم هَجْرًا جَمِيلا﴾ ("And be patient over what they say and avoid them with gracious avoidance"): this indicates — and Allah knows best — [that it was] before the Muslims were commanded to fight.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿وَذَرْنِي والمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ ومَهِّلْهم قَلِيلا﴾ ("And leave Me with the deniers, the possessors of ease, and give them respite a little"); and similar to it is ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11] ("Leave Me with the one I created alone").
If someone says: what is the sense of «ذَرْنِي» ("leave Me"), when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does whatever He wills, and no barrier stands between Him and His will? The answer to that is that when the Arabs want to tell a person that they are intent upon some matter or some person, they say «دَعْنِي وزَيْدًا» ("leave me and Zayd") — not that anyone is standing between him and Zayd; rather its interpretation is: "Do not concern yourself with Zayd, for I shall deal with him for you."

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَدَيْنا أنْكالا وجَحِيمًا﴾ ("Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire"): the singular of «الأنْكال» is «نِكْل», and it has come in the exegesis that here it means fetters of fire.
﴿وَطَعامًا ذا غُصَّةٍ وعَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 13] ("and food that chokes, and a painful punishment"): their food is ḍarīʿ, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهم طَعامٌ إلا مِن ضَرِيعٍ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 6] ("They will have no food except from ḍarīʿ"); it is shibriq, a thorny plant like boxthorn.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الأرْضُ والجِبالُ وكانَتِ الجِبالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلا﴾ ("On the Day the earth and the mountains will convulse, and the mountains will become a heap of sand pouring down"): «يَوْمَ» is accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿إنَّ لَدَيْنا أنْكالا وجَحِيمًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 12] ("Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire"), i.e. "the unbelievers will be made an example of, and He will punish them, on the Day the earth and the mountains convulse." «تَرْجُفُ» means: it will be shaken and moved with the most violent movement.
﴿وَكانَتِ الجِبالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلا﴾: the plural of «الكَثِيب» is «الكُثْبان», which are great masses of sand. The meaning of ﴿مَهِيلا﴾ is flowing, made to pour. The original of «مَهِيل» is «مَهْيُول»; one says «تُرابٌ مَهِيلٌ» and «تُرابٌ مَهْيُولٌ», i.e. poured out, made to flow, and «مَهِيل» is more common. The wāw was dropped only because the ḍamma is removed from the yāʾ in «مَهْيُول», so it and the wāw are quiescent, and the wāw is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. We have explained this in a similar place at greater length than this explanation, and we have kept it brief here in view of what preceded, because the grammarians disagree about it and its explanation would be long in this book.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ أخْذًا وبِيلا﴾ ("So We seized him with a ruinous seizure"): «الوَبِيل» is the very heavy and severe; from this, heavy, great rain is called «وابِل».

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ شِيبًا﴾ ("Then how can you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will make children white-haired?"): the meaning is "How can you guard yourselves against a Day that will make children white-haired, if you disbelieve", i.e. by what will you be protected from Allah's punishment on a Day from whose terror the young turn grey without old age, every nursing mother forgets what she nursed, and you see people drunk though they are not drunk — but the punishment of Allah is severe. Then He described, of the terror of that Day, that He said: ﴿السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18] ("the sky will be split thereby"), i.e. the sky will be split open by it, as He said: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 1] ("When the sky is split open"). And it was said in the exegesis: ﴿السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18], i.e. the sky will be weighed down by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ ("split thereby"), and He did not say «مُنْفَطِرَةٌ» — though «مُنْفَطِرَةٌ» is permissible, and on that came ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 1] ("When the sky breaks apart"); but it is not permissible to read in this place «السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرَةٌ», because it contradicts the Muṣḥaf. The masculine is on two lines. One of them is on the meaning that «السَّماء» means the roof; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا السَّماءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 32] ("And We made the sky a protected roof"). The second line is on [the model of] the saying «اِمْرَأةٌ مُرْضِعٌ» ("a suckling woman"), i.e. by way of attribution (nasab): the meaning is "the sky, possessed of splitting", as you say «اِمْرَأةٌ مُرْضِعٌ», i.e. "possessed of suckling".
And His saying: ﴿أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11] ("possessors of ease"): «النَّعْمَة» is luxurious living, and «النِّعْمَة» is the kindly favour done to a person, and the beneficence of Allah the Exalted. Had it been read «أُولِي النِّعْمَةِ», it would have been a valid line, because those on whom favour is bestowed may be believers or non-believers; Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿صِراطَ الَّذِينَ أنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fātiḥa: 7] ("the path of those You have favoured, not of those who incurred wrath").
[Translator's note: the source writes both words as «اَلنَّعْمَةُ»; the second, glossed as "favour", is evidently «النِّعْمَة» with kasra and is rendered so.]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما تُقَدِّمُوا لأنْفُسِكم مِن خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هو خَيْرًا وأعْظَمَ أجْرًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20] ("And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward"): its meaning is "better for you than the enjoyment of this world". «خَيْرًا» is accusative, the second mafʿūl (object) of «تَجِدُوهُ», and «هُوَ» came in as a separating pronoun (faṣl). We have explained that earlier in the book. Had it been outside the Qur'an, «تَجِدُوهُ هو خَيْرٌ» would be permissible, so that you would make it nominative with «هُوَ» [as mubtadaʾ]; but the accusative is better in Arabic, and nothing else is permissible in the Qur'an.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أنَّكَ تَقُومُ أدْنى مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ ونِصْفَهُ وثُلُثَهُ﴾ ("Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it"). Whoever reads ﴿نِصْفَهُ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] in the accusative, and ﴿وَثُلُثَهُ﴾, it is clear and good: it is an explanation of the measure of his standing, because when He said ﴿أدْنى مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ﴾ ("nearly two-thirds of the night"), "half of it" was an explanation of that "nearly". Whoever reads «وَنِصْفِهِ وثُلُثِهِ» (genitive), the meaning is: "and you stand less than half of it and than a third of it."

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلا ثَقِيلا﴾ ("Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word"). It has come in the exegesis that acting upon it is heavy, because the lawful and the unlawful, prayer and fasting, and everything Allah has commanded to be done and has forbidden — no one carries it out except by undertaking what is heavy for him. And it is possible, according to the doctrine of the lexicographers, that its meaning is that it is a word that has weight in its soundness, its clarity and its benefit, as you say «هَذا كَلامٌ رَصِينٌ» ("this is weighty speech") and «هَذا قَوْلٌ لَهُ وزْنٌ» ("this is a statement that has weight") when you consider it excellent and know that it has hit the mark of wisdom and clarity.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هي أشَدُّ وطْئًا﴾ ("Indeed, the rising by night is firmer in waṭʾ") — and it is read «وَطاءً» — ﴿وَأقْوَمُ قِيلا﴾ ("and more upright in speech"). «ناشِئَةُ اللَّيْلِ» are all the hours of the night, whenever any of it arises; i.e. everything that occurs of it is a nāshiʾa. The meaning of «هِيَ أشَدُّ وطْئًا» is: it is more in harmony (muwāṭaʾa) with the turning of the hearing. Whoever reads ﴿وَطْئًا﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw, its meaning is: it is more effective in standing [in prayer] and clearer in speech. It is possible that «أشَدُّ وطْئًا» means: heavier upon a person than standing by day, because the night was made for rest. And it was said: «أشَدُّ وطْئًا», i.e. greater in reward, because the reward of everyone who strives is in proportion to his striving.
[Translator's note: «لِتَقَلُّبِ السَّمْعِ» ("the turning of the hearing") may be a corruption of «لِلْقَلْبِ والسَّمْعِ» ("the heart and the hearing"). Also, the text says the reading with fatḥa on the wāw (waṭʾan) gives the second sense; the variant mentioned earlier is «وِطاءً», so the vowelling may be disturbed. Both translated as written.]

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَكَ في النَّهارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلا﴾ ("Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation") means: long free time and long scope for going about.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿واذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And remember the name of your Lord"), i.e. if you miss anything of the night, you have free time in the day.
It was also read «سَبْخًا» with the dotted khāʾ, while the [established] reading is with the undotted ḥāʾ. The meaning of «سَبْخًا» is sound in the language: a piece of cotton is called «سَبْخَة», and one says «سَبَخْتُ القُطْنَ» meaning «نَفَشْتُهُ» ("I teased the cotton out"), and the meaning of «نَفَشْتُهُ» is "I spread it out". So the meaning on that basis is: "Indeed, for you by day is long room for ease", and its meaning is close to the meaning of «السَّبْح».
﴿واذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وتَبَتَّلْ إلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلا﴾ ("And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion"): the meaning is "remember the name of your Lord by day". The meaning of ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ إلَيْهِ﴾ is: cut yourself off [from all else] to Him in worship. From this Mary (peace be upon her) was called «البَتُول», because she cut herself off to Allah, exalted be His praise, in worship; and likewise «صَدَقَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ» is an alms cut off from the property of the almsgiver and going out to the ways of Allah. The original form of the maṣdar of «تَبَتَّلَ» is «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبَتُّلًا», and «بَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا»; so «تَبْتِيلًا» is construed according to the meaning of "devote yourself to Him with complete devotion".
[Translator's note: the source prints «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا» and «بَتِلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا»; the argument requires «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبَتُّلًا» and «بَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا», which is how it is rendered above.]

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فاتَّخِذْهُ وكِيلا﴾ ("so take Him as Disposer of affairs"), i.e. take Him as guarantor of what He has promised you.
